title: FROM FINANCIAL REPORTING TO ALGORITHMIC REPORTING: EXPANDING THE SCOPE OF ACCOUNTABILITY IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
summary: In the context of the rapidly evolving digital economy, data and algorithms are increasingly becoming critical drivers of enterprise value creation and operational efficiency. However, existing accounting and reporting systems continue to focus primarily on tangible assets and financial flows, thereby failing to adequately capture the role of digital assets and algorithmic models. This study employs a qualitative research approach based on a systematic literature review, comparative analysis of international regulatory frameworks, and secondary data analysis to examine the limitations of traditional financial reporting and explore the role of algorithm reporting in enhancing corporate accountability. The analysis focuses primarily on the Vietnamese context while drawing upon international governance experiences during the period 2019–2024, when AI adoption and digital transformation accelerated significantly. The study proposes an expansion of the scope of accountability from traditional financial reporting to algorithm reporting, with the aim of enhancing transparency, responsibility, and control within the digital economy. Theoretically, the study contributes to the emerging literature by extending the concept of accountability beyond financial disclosure to include algorithmic governance and digital resources. Practically, it proposes an integrated algorithm reporting framework and policy recommendations that support the modernization of accounting standards, AI governance, and auditing practices in Vietnam.

title: The Mediating Role of Big Data Adoption on the Relationship between Board Governance and Audit Report Lag: Empirical Evidence from Indonesian Listed Companies
summary: Timely audited financial reporting is essential for capital market transparency, especially as companies increasingly operate in a data-intensive business environment. This study examine whether Big Data Adoption (BDA) mediates the relationship between Board Governance and Audit Report Lag (ARL) in companies in the technology, telecommunications, and healthcare sectors listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2019–2024 period. Using 294 firm-year observations, this study applies panel regression, Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to test direct and indirect effects among the variables. The results indicate that BDA has a significant negative effect on ARL, suggesting that companies with higher levels of BDA tend to complete audits more quickly. BDA also significantly mediates the relationship between board size and ARL, and between board expertise and ARL. However, BDA was not found to mediate the relationship between board independence and ARL or between Board Diversity and ARL. This study extends the literature on corporate governance, audit timeliness, and digital transformation by demonstrating that board governance can reduce audit delays when supported by data-driven capabilities. These findings also provide practical implications for companies, auditors, and regulators seeking to improve audit readiness, reporting efficiency, and digital governance.

title: Green Investment, Environmental, Social and Governance Disclosures, and Corporate Social Responsibility: The Case of Nigerian Companies
summary: Existing research provides little evidence that investments with an environmental focus promote better corporate social responsibility (CSR) practices or are simply symbolic actions in weak institutional environments. Hence, this study investigated the effect of green investment and ESG disclosures on the CSR performance of listed companies in Nigeria. The research was grounded in stakeholder and institutional theories to explain the relationship between environmentally driven investments and corporate social outcomes. Secondary data was collected from annual reports of selected listed companies for ten years and analysed using the Feasible Generalised Least Squares (FGLS) and Driscoll-Kraay Standard Error (DKSE) estimation techniques. The findings revealed that green investment has a positive and significant impact on CSR practices (Z = 4.849, p < 0.01). This implies that companies with higher green investment practices have more participation in environmental protection, community development, and responsible governance. The results also suggested that supporting factors such as green capital expenditure, ESG initiatives, green technological innovation, and carbon emission reduction efforts have an influence on the success of green investment. The study found that green investment improves CSR performance; however, its effect may be reduced to a legitimacy tool where institutional structures are weak. The research indicates that policymakers should tighten sustainability regulations and foster transparent ESG reporting. At the same time, companies should connect green investment to long-term environmental and social strategies to achieve meaningful CSR outcomes.

title: Examining the Role of Corporate Governance and ESG in Curbing Energy Intensity of Indian Manufacturing Firms: An ESG Greenwashing Perspective
summary: ABSTRACT The current study centres on assessing the impact of corporate governance and ESG on the energy intensity of manufacturing firms in an Indian setting. Specifically, we examine whether the ESG mechanism aids in enhancing environmental sustainability practices or contributes to corporate greenwashing. We use a panel dataset of 325 listed Indian manufacturing firms for the period spanning from 2011 to 2023 and employ the two‐step system GMM method for empirical analysis. We exhibit that corporate governance is efficacious in minimising the firm‐level energy intensity. On the contrary, the ESG mechanism fails to reflect higher energy efficiency as it holds a positive nexus with energy intensity. Our study confirms evidence of greenwashing behaviour linked to Indian manufacturing firms through ESG. We discern that the ESG mechanism is strategically used to mislead customers and investors and reflects a mere symbolic action of sustainability reporting. Heeding such study outcomes, we provide policy suggestions for improving ESG as well as the environmental sustainability framework for Indian manufacturing firms.

title: Investigation of the Impact of Digital Twin Technology on Strategic Supply Chain Resilience and Enterprise Operational Performance
summary: The turbulent global economy has witnessed abrupt fluctuations and repeated crises, fundamentally altering the operating modes of energy enterprises.Given recent environmental volatility, digital twin technology has emerged as a critical tool to enhance supply chain systems.Although conceptual studies on digitalization are abundant, empirical evidence detailing how digital twin technologies improve enterprise operations remains insufficient.Adopting the Dynamic Capabilities View, this paper establishes a moderated mediation model and conducts empirical research using a stratified sample of 342 senior operating managers and supply chain directors in the energy sector.Using partial least squares structural equation modeling, the empirical results indicate that digital twin technologies directly promote the improvement of operational performance.Furthermore, strategic supply chain resilience partially mediates this relationship.Additionally, the results demonstrate that environmental dynamism moderates these indirect paths; notably, the strategic value of digital twin technology is amplified under conditions of high market volatility.This study provides new theoretical support for supply chain management and offers a practical model for managers to build resilience and improve performance in high-volatility environments.

title: IT-Enabled Supply Chain Resilience in Global Logistics Operations: A Scenario-Based Informatics and Service-System Coordination Framework
summary: Global supply chains are highly interconnected -material flows, information flows, digital platforms, suppliers, logistics providers, and customers are more and more interdependent with each other in the form of logistics service systems.In times of geopolitical uncertainty, a pandemic outbreak, cyber threats, demand fluctuations and technological downtime, supply chain resilience goes beyond flexibility and redundancy of resources.It demands a comprehensive logistics informatics system, an instant service coordination and adaptive digital decision-making.This study constructs an IT-supported supply chain resilience model, which combines enterprise resource planning systems, Internet of Things monitoring, cloud platforms, blockchain traceability, big data analytics and digital twin technologies.The research uses scenario analysis to assess the impact of digital integration on recovery time, lead time, transparency and adaptability and service continuity in global logistics operations.The empirical framework is based on selected multinational companies and the indicators of resilience are the Index of Digitalization of Supply Chains, Scenario Stability Unit and Index of Supply Chain Adaptability.Results indicate that digitally integrated logistics systems are more resilient in the event of an economic shock and technology failure, as well as combined disruptions.The highest resilience effect is realized when IT tools are used as an integrated service-system architecture as opposed to individual technological services.In this study, an integrated model for digital coordination of resilient supply chain operations is proposed, which is also a contribution to the field of logistics informatics and service science.

title: CSR and Green Knowledge Management as Drivers of Sustainable Performance: The Mediating Role of Green Innovation and the Moderating Effect of Top Management Commitment
summary: ABSTRACT In recent years, the dual pressures of economic development and environmental degradation have intensified the need for organizations to adopt environmentally sustainable practices. In this context, corporate social responsibility (CSR), green knowledge management (GKM), and green innovation (GI) have become critical mechanisms for enhancing sustainable performance, particularly within healthcare organizations operating in Palestine. Accordingly, this study seeks to examine the roles of CSR and GKM in shaping sustainable performance through the mediating influence of GI. In addition, the study evaluates the moderating effect of top management commitment (TMC) on the relationship between GI and sustainable performance. The proposed relationships are empirically tested using data collected from 181 respondents representing governmental and non‐governmental healthcare organizations in Palestine. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) is employed to assess the structural model and examine the hypothesized relationships. The findings reveal that CSR and GKM exert both direct and indirect effects on sustainable performance through GI. Notably, TMC does not significantly moderate the relationship between GI and sustainable performance. This finding suggests that, in resource‐constrained healthcare settings, managerial commitment alone may not be sufficient to strengthen the performance benefits associated with GI. One possible explanation is that the influence of managerial commitment depends on complementary organizational conditions, such as available resources, implementation capacity, delegated authority, and performance‐monitoring systems. Theoretically, the study identifies GI as an important complementary pathway through which CSR and GKM are associated with sustainable performance while showing that the role of TMC may be context‐dependent. Practically, the findings indicate that healthcare managers should complement leadership commitment with concrete implementation mechanisms. Contextually, the study extends sustainability research to Palestinian healthcare organizations operating under substantial resource and institutional constraints.

title: Digital transformation is associated with lower ecological footprint across developed and developing economies
summary: The rapid expansion of the digital economy is transforming global production and consumption systems, yet its environmental implications remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the relationship between the Digital Economy Index (DEI) and ecological footprint (EF) across 77 developed and developing countries from 2001 to 2020. An integrated empirical framework combining fixed-effects and System GMM estimation with machine learning techniques, Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Machine (SVM), is employed to provide complementary econometric and predictive evidence. Econometric results show that digitalization significantly reduces EF on average, with stronger environmental benefits observed in developed economies. Moderation analysis reveals that industrialization and trade openness weaken these environmental benefits, whereas artificial intelligence, ICT development, and renewable energy transitions strengthen them. The transmission-channel analysis further suggests that environmental technological innovation and changes in the energy structure may represent potential pathways linking digitalization to environmental outcomes. The machine learning analysis provides complementary predictive evidence and identifies a nonlinear pattern in the DEI–EF relationship, potentially exhibiting an inverted U-shape in which ecological pressure increases at earlier stages of digitalization but declines at more advanced stages. RF and SVM achieve predictive accuracies of 94% and 80%, respectively. Overall, the findings indicate that digitalization is not inherently green and that its environmental benefits depend on the stage of digital development and broader structural and technological conditions, highlighting the importance of clean energy integration and sustainable digital transformation.

title: Pengaruh Tax Avoidance, Tax Risk, dan Earnings Management terhadap Cost of Debt pada Perusahaan Sektor Consumer Non-Cyclicals
summary: This study aims to determine the effect of Tax Avoidance, Tax Risk, and Earnings Management on Cost of Debt in Consumer Non-Cyclicals sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the 2020–2025 period. The method used in this study is a quantitative method. The data used are secondary data in the form of published financial statements of Consumer Non-Cyclicals sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2020–2025 period. The sample was collected using the purposive sampling method. The number of companies used as research samples was 13 companies, with observations conducted over 6 years from 2020 to 2025, resulting in 78 observations, of which 4 observations were excluded as outliers, leaving 74 observations as the final sample. The data analysis techniques used in this study are panel data analysis, coefficient of determination, F-test, and t-test, assisted by EViews-12 software. The results show that Tax Avoidance has a regression coefficient of (β = −0.539567) with a probability value (p = 0.0003), indicating a negative and significant effect on Cost of Debt. Tax Risk has a coefficient of (β = 0.163195) with (p = 0.3762), and Earnings Management has a coefficient of (β = 0.051421) with (p = 0.7236), indicating that both variables have no significant effect on Cost of Debt. Simultaneously, the three variables have a significant effect on Cost of Debt, with an F-statistic value of (5.572562) and (p = 0.001736).

summary: The rapid development of digital technologies is transforming modern economies by creating new mechanisms of production, distribution, consumption, and public administration. This article examines the theoretical foundations and current trends of the digital economy, focusing on the experience of the Republic of Uzbekistan. Particular attention is given to the "Digital Uzbekistan – 2030" strategy, digital infrastructure, e-government, digital finance, e-commerce, the IT sector, and human capital development. The study applies systematic, comparative, and institutional approaches, as well as the analysis of statistical and regulatory information. The findings show that Uzbekistan has established important institutional and technological foundations for digital transformation. However, challenges remain, including the digital divide, a shortage of qualified specialists, cybersecurity risks, unequal regional access to digital infrastructure, and regulatory gaps. The study proposes strengthening digital infrastructure, developing digital skills, expanding the application of artificial intelligence and big data, supporting digital entrepreneurship, and promoting international digital integration. title: Digital transformation, traceability, and supply chain resilience in food manufacturing SMEs: a review of AI, blockchain-IoT, and institutional mechanisms
summary: Food supply chains in China face persistent challenges of food safety risks, inadequate transparency, and supply disruptions, with food manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) disproportionately vulnerable due to limited resources and non-standardized internal processes. Digital transformation encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, Internet of Things (IoT), and digital twin technologies is increasingly regarded as a strategic solution to strengthen supply chain resilience, yet the organizational and institutional conditions under which these digital investments translate into tangible resilience improvements for food manufacturing SMEs remain poorly understood. This review conducts a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and thematic synthesis of 40 multidisciplinary sources spanning the food safety, supply chain management, and information systems literatures. Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Institutional Theory, we propose an integrative conceptual framework comprising six research propositions, in which traceability capability acts as a food-safety-specific mediating mechanism linking digital transformation to supply chain resilience, while regulatory stringency moderates the strength of this indirect pathway. A central argument of this framework is that deploying blockchain, IoT, or AI hardware does not itself constitute traceability capability the institutional and organisational conditions under which digital tools are adopted determine whether firms build substantive traceability capability or engage in symbolic compliance without genuine food safety governance improvement. Three key contributions distinguish this framework: conceptualizing traceability capability as a distinct dynamic capability rather than a generic digitalization mechanism; directing analytical focus explicitly toward food manufacturing SMEs, a population largely overlooked in existing large-firm panel studies; and introducing regulatory stringency as a first-stage moderator within a moderated mediation structure. Critical research gaps are identified, including the absence of SME-calibrated digital transformation measurement instruments, the lack of a validated multi-item traceability capability scale, and a complete empirical vacuum for testing the proposed moderated mediation model in food manufacturing SME contexts. This review provides a structured future research agenda for scholars and delivers actionable insights for practitioners and policymakers seeking to direct digital technology investments toward improved food safety governance in China’s food manufacturing sector.

title: ESG Disclosure and Firm Profitability: The Moderating Roles of Firm Size and Corporate Governance
summary: The disclosure of Environmental, Social, and Governance practices has gained prominence as companies encounter heightened expectations from investors, regulators, and various stakeholders for enhanced transparency regarding their ESG activities. This study investigates the correlation between ESG disclosure and corporate profitability, focusing specifically on the moderating influence of company size. The study employs a quantitative methodology and uses purposive sampling to obtain 310 firm-year data points. Information was acquired via publicly accessible annual reports, sustainability documents, and ESG data sources. Corporate profitability is assessed using return on assets (ROA), whereas ESG transparency serves as the primary explanatory variable. The size of the firm is analyzed as a moderating variable, while firm age, leverage, revenue, and market capitalization are considered as control factors. Pearson correlation and moderated regression analysis were used to investigate the proposed relationships. The results indicate a negative and statistically significant correlation between ESG disclosure and profitability. The regression findings indicate a negative correlation between ESG disclosure and ROA (β = −0.116; t = −3.331), failing to substantiate the claim that ESG disclosure enhances profitability. The negative correlation persists as significant even after incorporating firm size into the model (β = −0.117; t = −3.245). The relationship between ESG disclosure and firm size is both positive and statistically significant (β = 0.118; t = 2.768), suggesting that firm size influences the ESG–profitability relationship. The negative correlation between ESG disclosure and profitability decrease with the growth of corporate size. The results indicate that the economic impacts of ESG disclosure vary among companies. Increased ESG disclosure correlates with decreased short-term accounting profitability; however, larger corporations seem more capable of managing the costs linked to ESG implementation and reporting, thereby mitigating negative profitability effects. The research thus illustrates that the size of a corporation is a significant variable in understanding the ESG–profitability relationship. The results bear significance for corporate executives, investors, and regulators. Managers must include ESG initiatives in overarching financial and operational strategies instead of regarding ESG disclosure as an isolated compliance task.

title: How Environmental, Social, and Governance Mediates the Impact of FinTech Investments on Bank Performance in Gulf Countries
summary: This study examines the FinTech factors affecting bank performance in Gulf countries. The study followed a causal research design employing data from 2010 to 2023. The study unit of analysis is twelve banks in Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia. The study also uses PLS-SEM because of its advantage in examining mediating pathways that might be obscured in simpler regression analyses. According to the study’s findings, FinTech factors such as mobile banking applications (MBA) and GDP per capita variables have a negative, statistically significant effect on bank performance. On the other hand, GDP per capita has not statistically positively affected both ROA and ROE of bank performance. Moreover, both MBA and GDP per capita directly enhance environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance. The ESG does affect ROE. Besides, ESG plays a mediating role by strengthening the relationship between MBA, GDP per capita, and ROE, as it enhances banks ESG performance. The current study fills a gap in the body of literature since it considers previously overlooked factors that affect bank performance, i.e., FinTech variables and the mediating role of ESG on their effects on bank performance. The resulting policy implication is that banks in Gulf countries benefit most from investing in FinTech innovation since they can enhance operational efficiency and support sustainability efforts by driving better ESG performance, ultimately fostering long term stability and growth in the banking sector.

title: The Moderating Effect of Board Diversity on the Environmental Disclosure and Earnings Management Relationship
summary: This study examines the moderating effect of board diversity on the relationship between corporate environmental disclosure (CED) and earnings management (EM) among 258 Bursa Malaysia-listed manufacturing companies from 2018 to 2023. Board diversity comprises gender diversity and accounting and financial competency. CED is measured using a 41-item content-analysis index, while EM includes accrual-based measures (Modified Jones and Kothari models) and real EM measures (abnormal production costs, operating cash flows and discretionary expenses). Using the generalised method of moments, the findings show that both board gender diversity and board competency significantly moderate the CED–EM relationship. Female board representation generally weakens the association between CED and accrual-based EM, although its effect on real EM vary across measures. Board competency also significantly conditions the relationship across accrual and real EM measures. The findings demonstrate that board composition shapes the relationship between environmental transparency and managerial reporting behaviour, and provide implications for strengthening corporate governance, reporting transparency and environmental accountability.

title: Mechanisms and Configurational Paths to Supply Chain Resilience in New Energy Vehicle Battery Companies Under Digital Transformation: An Integrated SEM and fsQCA Approach
summary: Batteries are the core component of new energy vehicles (NEVs), and their supply chain resilience matters for the sustainable development of the industry. Using 326 valid questionnaires completed by employees of NEV battery companies in Fujian, Guangdong and Jiangxi, structural equation modeling (SEM) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) were applied to examine how digital transformation, the three dimensions of supply chain dynamic capabilities (learning and absorption, innovation, and collaboration), and environmental dynamics are associated with supply chain resilience. Digital transformation is significantly and positively associated with resilience, both directly and indirectly through supply chain dynamic capabilities, which account for 47.09% of the total effect; collaboration carries the largest share among the three dimensions (34.66%). Environmental dynamics positively moderates this association. Necessity analysis indicates that no single antecedent condition is necessary for high resilience, while four configurations sufficient for high resilience were identified and summarized as three patterns, with a solution consistency of 0.877 and a solution coverage of 0.682. The pattern combining all three capability dimensions accounts for the largest share of membership in high resilience. High resilience therefore appears reachable through several functionally equivalent configurations rather than a single optimal combination of capabilities.

title: Communication Information Management in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises in Vietnam
summary: In the context of rapid digital transformation, information communication governance has increasingly become a critical managerial capability for enterprises, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). This study adopts an exploratory qualitative approach, integrating secondary data from reports, policy documents, and academic literature with primary data collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews with six experts experienced in business management, digital communication, and digital transformation. The findings indicate that the participating experts consistently emphasized the important role of information communication governance in enhancing decision-making quality, ensuring brand consistency, strengthening internal coordination, and mitigating communication-related risks. The study also suggests several major challenges currently faced by SMEs, including limited governance awareness, fragmented data management, shortages of interdisciplinary human resources, and increasing pressure to comply with legal and regulatory requirements. title: The Controlling Effect of Corporate Governance on Human Resource Accounting and Firm Value: Evidence from Quoted Manufacturing Firms in Nigeria
summary: This study investigated how corporate governance moderates the effect of human resource accounting on market value added of quoted manufacturing firms in Nigeria. Using panel data and linear regression with PCSEs, salaries and wages (LSW) showed a significant positive effect on firm value, while training and development costs (LTDC) were positive but insignificant. Board independence (BI) and audit committee independence (ACI) revealed negative insignificant associations, reflecting a conservative influence on value creation. Diagnostic tests confirmed the suitability of the random effects model with robust corrections. The overall models were statistically significant, though with modest explanatory power (R² = 0.064). The null hypothesis was rejected, confirming corporate governance as a significant moderator. The study underscores the importance of human resource accounting and governance structures in enhancing firm value and provides insights for managers, policymakers, and researchers.

title: Considerations Regarding the Reconfiguration of the Financial-Accounting Ecosystem in the Context of Modern Digital Technologies
summary: Recent digital transformations are redefining the way the financial-accounting ecosystem operates as a result of the integration of ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) systems and artificial intelligence in accounting, auditing and sustainability reporting processes. As a result of increasing transparency requirements, the adoption of European standards on sustainability reporting and the rapid development of the digital economy, organizations have had to intervene in the process of conducting business, by rethinking operational models and governance mechanisms. The article aims to analyze how the use of ERP systems and artificial intelligence can contribute to the reconfiguration of the financial-accounting ecosystem, facilitating augmented accounting, intelligent auditing and integrated reporting oriented towards economic, environmental and social performance. The objective of the paper is to identify the main opportunities and challenges generated by the integration of ERP systems and artificial intelligence in the financial and accounting activities undertaken by organizations, as well as to highlight the impact on the accounting profession and the decision-making process. The research method used to quantify the key findings relevant to the topic of this article was qualitative, focusing on the responses received from various respondents during interviews conducted with them. The results indicated a high degree of satisfaction of users in the financial-accounting field regarding the generation and analysis of financial and non-financial information, as well as the automation of repetitive activities, the detection of various anomalies and risks, and the monitoring of ESG indicators. The results also highlighted the standardization of data collection processes, the integration of financial and non-financial information into a single platform, the development of digital skills of accounting professionals and auditors, and the promotion of an organizational culture favorable to innovation and change. Thus, the study proposed in this article focuses on providing relevant information for both academia and practitioners or specialists in the financial-accounting and auditing fields regarding the building of intelligent, resilient and sustainable development-oriented organizations.

title: Can the green intellectual capital dimension, in conjunction with fintech adoption, achieve business sustainability?
summary: MSMEs are important pillars of the Indonesian economy as economic drivers, but they also have social and environmental responsibilities in supporting sustainable development. This study aims to analyze the green intellectual capital model, which not only considers profits but also contributes to environmental sustainability by leveraging fintech, thereby achieving business sustainability across economic, social, and environmental dimensions. This research method uses a quantitative approach, collecting primary data through questionnaires and analyzing them using SEM-PLS, with a sample of 220 businesses. The results of the study indicate that green intellectual capital has a significant influence on fintech adoption and on sustainability performance in all aspects, i.e., economic, social, and environmental. Fintech adoption has a significant influence on economic and social sustainability performance, but not significantly on environmental performance. Fintech adoption can mediate the effect of green intellectual capital on economic and social performance. Still, it cannot mediate the effect of green intellectual capital on environmental performance among MSMEs in the Serikat Usaha Muhammadiyah (SUMU) community of East Java. To achieve scale-up for MSMEs, specific policies are needed to direct the use of green fintech in company operations, thereby achieving a significant impact in realizing sustainable businesses, such as the use of environmentally friendly raw materials and products, energy efficiency, and access to green financing.

title: Environmental, Social and Governance Performance and Firm Value: A Bibliometric Review of Intellectual Structure and Emerging Research Trends (2015-2025)
summary: The issues of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factors have gained much attention in terms of firm valuation and investment decisions. Although ESG has been extensively studied over the years, there is a lack of understanding in terms of the intellectual structure and thematic development of the relationship between ESG and firm value. To bridge this gap, this paper seeks to conduct a bibliometric analysis of the body of literature about ESG–firm value relationships from the year 2015 to 2025. The research will utilise a data set of 589 journal papers that were retrieved from the Scopus database for the purpose of investigating the publication dynamics, prominent contributors, citation network, and the intellectual/conceptual structure of the field. From the analysis of the science mapping results, it can be deduced that there are four major streams of research: (1) relationship between ESG performance and firm value; (2) sustainability disclosures and transparency; (3) corporate governance structure; and (4) consequences of ESG factors on financial performance such as cost of capital and investment efficiency. In addition, through co-citations and bibliographic coupling, it is evident that the theories upon which the body of knowledge is built include not only finance but also stakeholder theory, agency theory, and sustainable perspectives. The contribution of this paper to the literature on ESG-firm value lies in synthesizing the existing works on the subject matter.

title: The Effects of Corporate Social Responsibility and Good Corporate Governance on Firm Value, with Profitability as a Moderating Variable
summary: This study examines the effect of corporate social responsibility (CSR) disclosure, managerial ownership, and institutional ownership on firm value, with profitability (ROA) as a moderating variable, in food and beverage companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024. Using a purposive sample of 16 firms (80 firm-year observations) and panel data regression with the Fixed Effects Model, the results show that CSR disclosure has a significant negative effect on firm value (β = −0.416802, p = 0.0095), managerial ownership has a significant positive effect (β = 0.155062, p = 0.0026), while institutional ownership shows no significant effect (β = −2.035018, p = 0.2957). CSR, managerial ownership, and institutional ownership jointly affect firm value (F = 10.99921, p = 0.000000, adjusted R² = 0.706303). Profitability significantly moderates the CSR–firm value relationship (β = 0.015940, p = 0.0358): because the CSR main effect is negative (β = −0.416802), this positive interaction indicates that profitability offsets part of the negative CSR effect rather than reversing it. Profitability does not significantly moderate the effect of managerial or institutional ownership on firm value. This study contributes to the CSR–firm value literature by distinguishing an offsetting moderation pattern from a reinforcing one, within a single sector (food and beverage) and post-pandemic period (2020–2024) not extensively covered in prior moderation studies.

title: GREEN FINANCE AND SME INCLUSION IN ZIMBABWE: EVIDENCE FROM THE MANUFACTURING SECTOR IN BINDURA
summary: Green finance is increasingly recognized as a central instrument for advancing climate mitigation and sustainable development, yet its distributive effects remain poorly understood in developing economies where small and medium enterprises (SMEs) dominate industrial activity. This study examines access to green finance among manufacturing SMEs in Bindura, Zimbabwe, identifying the structural determinants of inclusion and the institutional mechanisms driving exclusion. A mixed-methods approach is employed, combining quantitative survey data from 36 manufacturing firms analyzed through binary logistic regression with qualitative evidence from key informant interviews with financial institutions and policy actors. The results reveal that green finance access is highly selective: firm size, collateral availability, and awareness are significant positive predictors of access, while smaller and asset-constrained firms are systematically excluded. Green finance is predominantly delivered through conventional asset-based lending models underpinned by risk perceptions that disadvantage SMEs, reinforcing credit rationing and information asymmetry. These findings challenge the assumption that green finance is inherently inclusive and suggest that current frameworks risk entrenching a dual transition in which only better-positioned firms participate. Policy reforms should prioritize risk-sharing mechanisms, SME-adapted financial instruments, and targeted information dissemination to ensure a more equitable and effective green transition.

title: Corporate social responsibility incentives in supply chains under pricing authority: The role of reverse factoring
summary: Reverse factoring is a buyer-led supply chain finance mechanism that can alleviate the financial constraints faced by small and medium-sized suppliers and improve their capacity to invest in corporate social responsibility (CSR). However, improved access to financing does not necessarily translate into CSR investment, because the supplier’s incentive also depends on the allocation of wholesale-pricing authority and its ability to retain the returns generated by CSR. We develop an analytical model of a two-tier supply chain under demand uncertainty that integrates reverse factoring, endogenous wholesale pricing, order quantity, and supplier CSR effort. We compare two pricing structures: supplier-led pricing, in which the supplier determines the wholesale price and CSR effort, and retailer-led pricing, in which the retailer sets the wholesale price before the supplier chooses CSR effort. The results show that reverse factoring reduces financing-inclusive production and CSR costs, thereby improving the financial feasibility of CSR investment. Nevertheless, positive CSR effort depends on threshold conditions involving CSR effectiveness, CSR cost, production cost, and supplier margin. Supplier-led pricing generally supports CSR investment over a wider parameter region and induces higher CSR effort because the supplier can retain a larger share of the demand-enhancing value CSR generates. Under retailer-led pricing, wholesale-price compression may offset the financing benefit and reduce or eliminate the supplier’s incentive to invest. These findings demonstrate that the sustainability impact of reverse factoring depends on its interaction with pricing authority and surplus allocation. Managers should therefore coordinate financing arrangements with wholesale-pricing policies that preserve sufficient supplier incentives while maintaining overall supply chain performance.

title: The Fourth Chokepoint: Administrative Standardization as Process Control in China's Rare Earth Separation Industry
summary: Earlier work on rare earth supply chain resilience identifies three chokepoints, geology, processing capital expenditure, and separation learning curves. This preprint proposes a fourth, administrative control of the process envelope, meaning who may run a separation cascade, at what volume, on which feed, to which technical reference, under whose data, and with what permission to transfer know-how. Using public records from 2011 to October 2026, it describes six coupled layers of control in China's rare earth sector (volume, structure, technical envelope, information, boundary, and buffer) and maps them onto a process control analogy. Verified findings include the 2024 company level split of mining and separation quotas, the placement of the entire ion-adsorption mining quota in one company, the 2025 shift to undisclosed quotas and total volume control, and the concentration of imported feed in two border supply lines. The paper audits a broader compilation of reported mechanisms against public sources. Every claim is graded by evidence tier in an appendix, errors are corrected, and unverified items are listed as open requests for verification. The central thesis is presented as a hypothesis with rival explanations and falsifiable predictions, not as an established result. Corrections and primary sources are welcome.

title: Corporate Governance, Board Oversight, and Firm Value: Evidence from Listed Insurance Companies in Nigeria
summary: Effective board oversight is essential for corporate governance, accountability, and the sustainable value of firms. This study examines how board oversight functions relate to firm value and how this relationship has evolved among listed insurance companies in Nigeria. An ex post facto research design was employed, utilising secondary data from the annual reports and financial statements of 21 listed insurance companies from 2012 to 2021, resulting in 210 firm-year observations. Board oversight was assessed through audit committee, risk management, and remuneration governance functions, while firm value was measured using Market-to-Net Book Value (MNBV) and Tobin’s Q. Descriptive statistics, trend analysis, diagnostic tests, and regression analysis were conducted. The results show that firm value changed considerably throughout the period examined. Audit committee and remuneration governance functions demonstrated positive and statistically significant relationships with firm value, whereas risk management functions exhibited a negative and statistically significant relationship. These results suggest that strengthening board oversight mechanisms may improve, particularly risk management practices, to improve governance effectiveness and support sustainable firm value in Nigeria’s insurance industry.

title: Drivers of supply chain resilience: the roles of artificial intelligence, knowledge sharing, blockchain adoption and radical innovation capabilities
summary: Purpose Global supply chain dynamics have undergone significant changes due to economic uncertainty, logistical disruptions and large-scale crises. Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study examines the relationships among artificial intelligence, knowledge sharing, radical innovation capabilities, blockchain adoption and supply chain resilience. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 208 firms operating in Türkiye's foreign trade sector and analyzed using structural equation modeling and moderation analysis. Findings The results indicate that artificial intelligence facilitates knowledge sharing, which is positively associated with supply chain resilience. While knowledge sharing is significantly related to radical innovation capabilities, radical innovation capabilities do not exhibit a direct association with supply chain resilience. In addition, blockchain adoption strengthens the relationship between knowledge sharing and supply chain resilience, suggesting that blockchain enhances the effectiveness of knowledge-sharing mechanisms in fostering resilience. Originality/value This study contributes to the productivity and performance management literature by integrating digital technologies and knowledge-based capabilities within a unified framework to explain supply chain resilience from a dynamic capabilities perspective. The findings also provide practical insights for managers and policymakers by demonstrating that digital technologies alone may not generate resilience unless they are aligned with complementary organizational capabilities, such as knowledge sharing and innovation-oriented structures.

This research employed a quantitative approach using secondary data obtained from companies' annual reports and sustainability reports during the observation period. The sample was selected using a purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed using panel data regression with the Random Effect Model (REM), while the moderating effect was tested using Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The results indicate that Carbon Emission Disclosure has no significant effect on the Cost of Capital. Furthermore, Carbon Emission Intensity does not have a significant effect on the Cost of Capital. The moderation analysis also reveals that Carbon Emission Intensity does not moderate the relationship between Carbon Emission Disclosure and the Cost of Capital. These findings suggest that carbon emission disclosure and emission intensity have not yet become primary considerations for investors in determining the cost of capital of mining companies. Instead, investors tend to place greater emphasis on firms' fundamental factors, such as profitability, business risk, capital structure, and industry prospects, rather than environmental information when making investment decisions. This study contributes to the literature on environmental accounting and sustainable finance by providing empirical evidence regarding the relevance of carbon-related information in the Indonesian capital market.

title: The Integrative Role of the Audit Committee in Coordinating Internal Audit and External Audit
summary: This study examines the integrative role of the audit committee in coordinating internal audit and external audit functions within corporate governance systems. Although the academic literature has extensively analysed these assurance mechanisms, they are typically studied separately, and the conceptualisation of the audit committee as a coordination interface between them remains underdeveloped. The research employs the Structured Literature Review (SLR) methodology, following the framework proposed by Massaro et al. (2016), to ensure transparency and rigour in the selection and synthesis of existing studies. Starting from an initial set of 310 articles indexed in the Web of Science database, a multi-stage filtering process led to a final sample of 25 relevant studies, of which 17 directly analyse the interaction among internal audit, external audit, and the audit committee. The results reveal the predominance of a structural monitoring perspective, with most studies analysing bilateral relationships between the audit committee and one of the two audit functions. Trilateral approaches that simultaneously integrate all three governance mechanisms remain limited. Based on the synthesis conducted, the study proposes a conceptual framework structured around three levels — structural inputs, integration mechanisms, and governance outcomes — which positions the audit committee as an active interface facilitating coordination between internal audit and external audit. The main contribution of the research lies in integrating fragmented streams of the specialised literature and in developing a conceptual model that highlights the potential integrative role of the audit committee in the assurance architecture, while also providing a basis for future empirical testing.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Financial Performance: The Mediating Role of Employee Engagement and the Moderating Role of Job Autonomy in Malaysian Manufacturing Firms
summary: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) has historically been treated as a discretionary activity outside the realm of strategic management. However, over time CSR has gained traction as a necessary addition to any organisation with positive impact on the firm’s bottom line. Despite this progress, how CSR affects financial performance is not well understood, especially in an emerging- market manufacturing setting. This study investigates CSR’s impact on financial performance for Malaysian manufacturing firms while testing employee engagement as a mediating variable and job autonomy as a moderating condition. Five hypotheses were formulated on the basis of Stakeholder Theory, Social Exchange Theory, and Self-Determination Theory; direct effects of CSR on employee engagement and financial performance, the indirect effect of employee engagement on financial performance, mediation of employee engagement, and moderation of job autonomy were investigated. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional design was utilised. Participants were Malaysian employees working in manufacturing firms who completed a questionnaire. 384 completed questionnaires were collected from a sample of 500 resulting in a response rate of 76.8%. Data were analysed through descriptive statistics, exploratory factor analysis, reliability analysis, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, and conditional process analysis with PROCESS Model 7 using 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Results found CSR to have a positive and significant effect on financial performance and employee engagement. Employee engagement had a positive and significant effect on financial performance and fully mediated the relationship between CSR and financial performance. Job autonomy was found to have no significant effect on the relationship between CSR and employee engagement but was found to have a positive and significant relationship with employee engagement. This study contributes to the field of CSR by providing evidence that employee engagement serves as an important internal mechanism through which responsible organisational practices affect financial performance. The findings of this study show that job design may play an important role in manufacturing contexts where there are more formal procedures and requirements for operation.

title: Rasch Model: Employment Transition in Malaysia Driven by Environmental, Social, and Governance-Driven Transformation and Sustainable Social Innovation
summary: Employment transition in Malaysia is undergoing significant change as organizations adapt to sustainability demands and shifting workforce dynamics for economic growth. This paper presents a pilot study investigating the influence of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) and sustainable social innovation on employee transition. The sample comprised 31 audit firms registered with the Malaysian Institute of Certified Public Accountants (MICPA). The research employed a quantitative survey design, with data analyzed using the Rasch measurement model to assess the validity and reliability of the instruments. Data were analyzed using the Rasch Rating Scale Model (RSM), with the Partial Credit Model (PCM) applied where response categories varied. Model evaluation included category functioning, item-person fit, and reliability and separation indices. Targeting was examined using Wright maps, while unidimensionality was assessed through principal component analysis (PCA) of residuals. Local item dependence and differential item functioning (DIF) were also explored to ensure measurement validity. The survey instrument was designed to capture three latent constructs: ESG adoption, SSI practices, and ET readiness. The results show strong psychometric properties, with person reliability of 0.82 and item reliability of 0.91, confirming consistency and structural soundness. Person and item separation indices of 2.11 and 3.15 further demonstrate the model's effectiveness in differentiating between ability levels and item difficulty. However, some misfit items and potential multidimensionality highlight areas for refinement. This study places ESG and sustainable social innovation in the context of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and focuses on their potential to create inclusive and sustainable solutions. Overall, the pilot study indicates that the measurement is valid and reliable, and therefore suitable for use in the main study.

title: Community Empowerment Education through Corporate Social Responsibility Programs: Strengthening Entrepreneurial Capacity and Sustainable Socio-Economic Independence
summary: This study aims to analyze the implementation strategy of PT Inkorincorp Velocity's Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) program in empowering local communities, channeling its impact on capacity building and independence of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) actors, and identifying development synergies built in Balikpapan City. This study uses a qualitative descriptive approach with a case study design. Data was collected through in-depth interviews with CSR management, local governments, and target MSME actors, which were strengthened by field observations and documentation studies. Data analysis was carried out using the interactive model Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña with data validity tests through triangulation of sources and techniques. The results of the study show that PT Inkorincorp Velocity applies an empowerment approach based on participatory needs assessment that changes the CSR paradigm from charitable philanthropy to sustainable community building. The implications of the program can be seen in increasing turnover, expanding digital market reach, as well as strengthening social capital and institutional independence of citizen business groups. In addition, the realization of the synergy of the Triple Helix partnership between the company, the Balikpapan City Government, and the local community that not only encourages inclusive economic growth but also strengthens the company's social license to operate. The study concludes that structured CSR integration programs with local potential are effective in transforming socio-economic vulnerabilities into competitive community self-reliance.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF E-INVOICES GENERATED FROM CASH REGISTERS (POS E-INVOICES): EXPERIENCES FROM EAST ASIA AND LESSONS FOR PROMOTING THE DIGITAL ECONOMY IN VIETNAM
summary: This paper examines the digital transformation of tax administration in Vietnam, with a focus on the mandatory implementation of electronic invoices generated from cash registers (POS e-invoicing) under Decree 70/2025/ND-CP. Although this policy is designed to enhance financial transparency and enable continuous transaction controls (CTC), its rapid rollout has encountered notable resistance from small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and business households. Drawing on the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework, the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), and recent policy reports and empirical studies from the 2025–2026 period, this study identifies key barriers to adoption. These include high compliance costs, Application Programming Interface (API) incompatibility between legacy accounting systems and tax platforms, and behavioural resistance to real-time financial transparency. To contextualize these challenges, the study conducts a structured comparative analysis of selected East Asian economies. The findings highlight the role of financial incentives in South Korea, centralized technological infrastructure in China, and a phased and flexible transition approach in Japan. Based on these insights, the paper argues that administrative mandates alone are insufficient to ensure effective implementation. It proposes a comprehensive policy framework for Vietnam that integrates technological standardization, targeted financial support, and behavioural incentive mechanisms. These measures are expected to reduce implementation frictions, enhance voluntary tax compliance, and support the sustainable development of the national digital economy.

title: Southern Solutions to Fill Gaps in Global Development and Climate Finance: How the World’s Most Vulnerable Countries Are Deepening a Fourth Wave of Public Banking
summary: This article addresses the question of what financial resources are available to the world’s most climate exposed and vulnerable countries, and how this fits within and contributes to the broader South-South financial landscape. It presents original empirical data and institutional analysis to show new trends where emerging Southern-led public banks and financial institutions are deepening and broadening the global financial architecture, and why they feel compelled to do it. Using data from the IMF, UNCTAD, and the FICS/Peking University Institute of New Structural Economics Public Banks Database the article argues that the most climate-exposed and vulnerable countries have the least available finance and pay the highest prices for it. These countries did not cause the climate crisis, they are among the most impacted by it, and they have the least resources to confront it. Nonetheless, this does not mean they can do nothing; this article aims to show how developing countries are taking the reins into their own hands in an effort to fill gaps and limitations of the global financial architecture. It maps the public development banks owned by the 74 members of the Vulnerable-20 grouping, alongside complementary, innovative, instruments and mechanisms being created by V-20 and a broader, overlapping, group of net borrower countries. The article identifies and nests these within a maturing “fourth wave” of South-South initiatives that began in the mid 2010’s with the largest BRICS economies. The incipient Borrowers Platform, launched in 2026 by net borrowing countries, could, if successful, represent the peak thus far in this evolution.

title: Advancing Digital Banking in Albania: Trust, Financial Literacy and Regulatory Readiness in the FinTech Ecosystem
summary: Digital transformation is reshaping banking systems worldwide, yet the pace and depth of adoption remain uneven across emerging financial markets. Albania has made visible progress in electronic payments, online banking access and regulatory alignment with European digital finance standards; however, the transition from formal access to sustained digital banking adoption remains incomplete. This study examines the factors influencing digital banking and FinTech adoption in Albania, with a specific focus on consumer trust, financial literacy, perceived barriers and regulatory readiness. The paper applies a mixed-methods research design. Quantitative data were collected through a structured consumer survey with 151 respondents and analyzed through descriptive statistics and Spearman correlation analysis. Qualitative evidence was gathered through 15 semi-structured interviews with representatives from commercial banks, electronic money institutions, public institutions, regulators, sectoral organizations and academic experts. Thematic analysis was used to identify common institutional, technological and regulatory patterns. The findings show that digital banking services are widely accessible, but usage intensity remains moderate. Weekly and monthly use are more common than daily use, while trust, financial knowledge and perceived barriers significantly shape adoption patterns. The correlation analysis indicates a positive relationship between financial knowledge and digital banking use, and a negative relationship between perceived barriers and usage. Interview findings reveal six major themes: digital transformation as a strategic priority, Bank–FinTech cooperation, regulatory adaptation, cybersecurity and data protection, financial education, and an optimistic but conditional outlook toward 2030. The study contributes to the literature on digital financial inclusion in emerging markets by integrating consumer-level evidence with institutional and regulatory perspectives. It argues that Albania’s digital banking transition requires not only technological investment, but also trust-building, digital financial education, cybersecurity, regulatory innovation and stronger cooperation between banks, FinTech actors, regulators and academia.

title: Dampak Kesulitan Keuangan terhadap Indikasi Praktik Greenwashing: Analisis Peran Mediasi Inovasi Hijau
summary: Greenwashing has become a critical issue in corporate sustainability implementation; however, research on the impact of financial distress on greenwashing remains limited and yields inconsistent results. This study addresses this gap by examining the role of green innovation as a mediating variable in the relationship between financial distress and greenwashing, drawing upon legitimacy theory and stakeholder theory. The study focuses on energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange from 2020 to 2024, utilizing a sample of 87 companies (comprising 267 observations after outlier removal). Secondary data were analyzed using multiple linear regression and path analysis. The results indicate that financial distress has no significant effect on either greenwashing indications or green innovation. Similarly, green innovation does not significantly affect greenwashing indications. Conversely, firm size was found to have a significant positive effect on greenwashing indications. These findings suggest that financial distress does not influence corporate greenwashing practices, and green innovation does not mediate the relationship between financial distress and greenwashing

title: A Cost-Based System Model for Data Asset Valuation: A Case Study of a Chinese Supply Chain Company
summary: In the digital economy, data have become a new factor of production, making a rigorous and feasible data asset valuation system a practical necessity. As the supply chain sector advances toward digitalization and intelligent transformation, data assets have become a key source of competitive advantage for supply chain companies. Based on the modified cost approach, this study develops a valuation system comprising three subsystems: cost reconstruction, return enhancement, and value adjustment. First, data asset input costs are aggregated and converted into replacement costs. The cost–expense profit ratio is then introduced to estimate a theoretical benchmark value incorporating operating returns. Four groups of influencing factors—data quality and scale, the data asset market, data asset application, and value realization risk—are incorporated. The analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation (FCE) are combined to derive a value adjustment coefficient. Finally, the coefficient is applied to the theoretical benchmark value to obtain the data asset value. The system is applied to Company G, a supply chain company in China, as a case study. The results show that the replacement cost is RMB 1,804,126, the value adjustment coefficient is 0.8371, and the final estimated value is RMB 1,529,111.80. Sensitivity analysis reveals that direct and indirect costs exhibit the highest sensitivity coefficients of 0.566 and 0.434, respectively, followed by data quality and scale and data asset application. This study contributes to the methodological development of differentiated data asset valuation from a value formation perspective and provides practical insights for identifying data asset management priorities in supply chain companies.

title: Consumer Protection in the Digital Economy Era: A Literature Analysis of E-Commerce Regulation in Indonesia
summary: The growth of Indonesia’s digital economy has driven a significant transformation in transaction patterns while posing new challenges regarding consumer protection. Although the Consumer Protection Law and Personal Data Protection Law have been passed, they are not considered optimal in responding to the complexity of the digital ecosystem. This research uses a descriptive qualitative approach based on a structured literature review combined with doctrinal legal analysis and thematic synthesis. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of consumer protection regulations in e-commerce transactions in Indonesia by examining legal studies, consumer behavior, and international regulatory comparisons through a literature review approach. The study’s results show that regulatory implementation weaknesses, low digital literacy, insufficiently standardized online dispute resolution mechanisms, and institutional enforcement and supervisory gaps remain important obstacles. Additionally, an overly rigid ex-ante regulatory approach has the potential to stifle digital innovation. Therefore, adaptive, participatory policy reformulation based on the principle of equitable consumer protection is needed.

title: The Impact of Governance on Bank Risk: The Case of Tunisia
summary: Purpose: This study examines the impact of corporate governance on bank risk in the Tunisian banking sector.Given the nature of banking activities, particularly deposit-taking and lending, banks are inherently exposed to various forms of risk that may affect their financial stability and performance.Corporate governance provides the institutional framework through which banks are directed, controlled, and held accountable, and may therefore play an important role in mitigating or influencing bank risk.Design/Methodology/Approach: The study employs two static panel-data models to investigate the relationship between corporate governance mechanisms and bank risk.The empirical analysis is based on a sample of 11 Tunisian banks over the period 2016-2025.Bank risk is measured using two indicators: non-performing loans (NPL) and the Z-score.The governance variables considered include gender diversity, board size, board independence, audit committee size, and ownership structure.Findings: The results indicate that several corporate governance mechanisms significantly affect bank risk in Tunisia.In particular, gender diversity, board size, and board independence have significant effects on bank risk, as measured by both NPL and the Zscore.In contrast, audit committee's size and ownership structure do not have a statistically significant effect on bank risk.Originality/Value: The study contributes to the literature on corporate governance and bank risk by providing empirical evidence from the Tunisian banking sector over a recent ten-year period.The findings highlight the importance of board characteristics, particularly gender diversity, board size, and board independence, in understanding variations in bank risk.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Tax Aggressiveness of Quoted Oil and Gas Firms in Nigeria
summary: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) involves firms voluntarily engaging in practices that promote social good, which often includes ethical business practices, environmental stewardship, and community engagement. Investigating how CSR commitments correlates with tax aggressiveness necessitated this study. The study examined corporate social responsibility and tax aggressiveness of quoted oil and gas firms in Nigeria. The population of the study consists of twelve (12) quoted oil and gas firms in Nigeria. Secondary data was obtained from the audited annual financial reports of the quoted oil and gas firms in Nigeria from 2014 - 2023. Hypotheses formulated were tested using panel least squares regression through pooled effect, fixed effect, and random effect, determined by the Hausman test, fixed effect regression was preferred for results interpretation with the aid of E-views 10 econometric statistical software. Findings shows that corporate donations and social cost is negative (-3.056199) and significant at (0.0000). This negative impact of DSOC led to reduction in effective tax rate which is favourable to tax aggressiveness while, environmental cost is negative (-0.014754) and insignificant at (0.4268) to effective tax rate. This connotes that a rise in EVC by 1 unit will cause effective tax rate to reduce by 0.014754. The adjusted R-squared of 0.642196 suggests that DSOC and EVC account for roughly 64.2% of the variation in ETR, with the remaining 35.8% attributed to other factors not considered in this study. The study concludes that donations, social costs and environmental cost were the factors of corporate social responsibility that led to a decrease in the effective tax rate. The study therefore, recommends that given the significant negative impact of social costs (Donations) on tax aggressiveness, companies may consider increasing their social responsibility initiatives. This will not only reduce their tax liability but also enhance their corporate image and stakeholder relations. Finally, since environmental costs do not show a significant impact on tax aggressiveness, companies should re-evaluate their environmental strategies to ensure they are effectively managing costs since there are no significant tax benefits.

title: Green is Queen: Do Female CEOs Promote Substantive Green Innovation or Tactical Green Innovation?
summary: ABSTRACT Green innovation serves as a pivotal strategy for firms to achieve sustainable development. Given the steadily increasing demand for female leadership in the firms, understanding how female CEOs impact green innovation has emerged as a critical area of inquiry. This study utilizes panel data from Chinese listed companies from 2012 to 2025 to empirically investigate how female CEOs impact different types of green innovation. The research findings indicate that female CEOs play a significant role in promoting substantive green innovation while simultaneously inhibiting tactical green innovation. From the perspective of time attention allocation, female CEOs exert differentiated impacts on green innovation by suppressing the senior executives' current attention and promoting their future attention. Furthermore, media environmental protection coverage exerts distinct moderation effects on the impact of female CEOs on the green innovation. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the impact of female CEOs on the two types of green innovation is more significant in state-owned enterprises, heavy-polluting industries, northern regions, and firms with longer female CEO tenure. This study contributes to the advancement of cross-theoretical research on leadership and corporate governance.

title: Beyond compliance: Embedding ethics in ESG reform for emerging economies
summary: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reforms are expanding across emerging economies, yet many initiatives struggle to achieve ethical legitimacy in practice. Prior research has emphasized the adoption of disclosure and the development of metrics, while offering a limited explanation of why ESG systems often remain vulnerable to symbolic compliance, exclusion, and trust deficits in institutionally constrained contexts. The study addresses this gap by examining how structural conditions shape the ethical quality of ESG governance, particularly in relation to fairness, accountability, legitimacy, inclusion, and rights. A qualitative, interpretive design was adopted, drawing on the analysis of 56 publicly available documents, including corporate ESG disclosures, regulatory and policy frameworks, and civil society assessments. NVivo-assisted thematic coding integrates ethics-informed deductive categories with inductive theme development to identify recurring barriers and their normative implications. The findings indicate that fragmented mandates create compliance ambiguity and privilege well-resourced incumbents, while weak enforcement mechanisms enable disclosure without substantive accountability. Trust deficits among investors, regulators, and local communities further undermine legitimacy, especially where stakeholder engagement is perceived as formalistic. In addition, infrastructure and data limitations restrict participation by smaller actors, and the growing digitization of ESG systems introduces under-regulated risks related to privacy and algorithmic opacity. The study reframes ESG reform in emerging economies as an ethical governance challenge and identifies adaptive pathways for building more credible, inclusive, and ethically robust ESG systems.

title: NAVIGATING DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION: THE INTERPLAY OF AMBIDEXTROUS LEADERSHIP, AGILITY, AND ORGANIZATIONAL RESILIENCE IN EMERGING MARKETS
summary: In an increasingly volatile, uncertain, complex, and ambiguous (VUCA) global environment, organizations face dual pressures to optimize existing operational capabilities while aggressively deploying digital innovations. This study investigates the structural mechanisms through which ambidextrous leadership drives sustainable organizational resilience via the mediating role of dynamic enterprise agility within emerging-market business enterprises. Anchored in the Dynamic Capabilities Framework and the Resource-Based View (RBV), we posit a structural model examining exploratory and exploitative leadership behaviors, process agility, market responsiveness, and multifaceted resilience (operational, financial, and strategic). Employing a cross-sectional, quantitative survey design, empirical data were gathered from N=412 senior executives, general managers, and chief technology officers across technology-enabled, manufacturing, and financial services firms in India. Structural Equation Modeling via Partial Least Squares (PLS-SEM) was utilized to test the hypothesized paths and mediation effects. The results demonstrate that ambidextrous leadership exerts a statistically significant positive effect on organizational resilience (=0.342,p<0.001) and enterprise agility (=0.584,p<0.001). Furthermore, enterprise agility significantly mediates the relationship between ambidextrous leadership and organizational resilience (=0.286,p<0.001), accounting for a substantial indirect effect. The findings provide practical and theoretical frameworks for enterprise leaders navigating digital transformations under UGC-CARE and global research benchmark criteria, highlighting that structural ambidexterity without dynamic process adaptation yields suboptimal long-term stability.

title: Design and Validation of a Performance Improvement Model Based on Social Responsibility Accounting
summary: The present study was conducted with the aim of designing and validating a performance improvement model based on social responsibility accounting in companies listed on the Tehran Stock Exchange. This research employed an exploratory mixed-methods approach implemented in two qualitative and quantitative phases. In the qualitative phase, using thematic analysis and semi-structured interviews with 20 theoretical and practical experts, the dimensions, components, and indicators of the model were identified. Test–retest reliability with a coefficient of 69% and intra-subject agreement between two coders confirmed the analytical rigor of this phase. In the quantitative phase, the extracted model was validated with the participation of 245 financial managers from listed companies using a 68-item questionnaire and structural equation modeling based on the partial least squares (PLS-SEM) approach. The findings indicated that the final model consisted of six principal constructs: “Corporate Social Accountability,” “Social Transparency and Disclosure,” “Accounting Identification and Measurement of Environmental Impacts,” “Environmental Accounting Reporting and Disclosure,” “Financial Performance,” and “Non-Financial Performance.” The path analysis results demonstrated the positive and significant effects of social accounting (path coefficient = 0.517) and environmental accounting (path coefficient = 0.715) on organizational performance. The coefficient of determination (R²) showed that these two paths jointly explained 72% of the variance in performance. Furthermore, hierarchical analysis ranked the dimensions, with “Social Transparency and Disclosure” and “Environmental Reporting” receiving the highest priorities, respectively. The satisfactory fit of the model was confirmed by a GOF index of 0.620 and an NFI value of 0.957. In addition, the internal and external validity of the model was endorsed by experts, with mean scores exceeding 4.20. The proposed model provides an operational framework for integrating social and environmental commitments into organizational performance management systems.

title: Thin capitalization and tax avoidance: The moderating role of independent commissioners
summary: This study examines the effect of thin capitalization on tax avoidance and the moderating role of independent commissioners in consumer non-cyclical companies in Indonesia. The study employs 150 firm-year observations from companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2021-2023. The hypotheses are tested using fixed-effects panel regression estimated via Generalized Least Squares (GLS) to address heteroskedasticity. The results indicate that thin capitalization has a positive effect on tax avoidance, while independent commissioners weaken this relationship. These findings suggest that debt financing provides firms with opportunities to reduce their tax burdens through interest deductions. In contrast, greater representation of independent commissioners may constrain the tax-related implications of financing decisions. This study contributes to the literature by highlighting the role of corporate governance in moderating the relationship between thin capitalization and tax avoidance. The findings also provide implications for the Directorate General of Taxes in strengthening risk-based supervision of debt-related tax deductions and corporate financing arrangements.

title: The Impact of Executives’ Overseas Background on Corporate ESG: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Companies
summary: Within the dual background of the “dual carbon” strategy and the standardized development of ESG in capital markets, exploring the driving mechanisms of corporate ESG performance is crucial, for promoting the sustainable operation of listed companies. This research takes Chinese A-share listed companies, from 2009 to 2023, as the research sample and, empirically analyzes the impact of executives’ overseas background on corporate ESG performance, based on upper echelons theory. The findings are concluded as follows: executives’ overseas background can boost a company’s overall ESG score, and remains valid after a series of robustness tests; mechanism tests indicate that executives’ overseas background can enhance corporate governance, thus improving corporate ESG performance; heterogeneity analysis indicates that this effect is more pronounced in non-state-owned enterprises, mature enterprises, and enterprises with lower levels of green innovation. This research provides empirical evidence for enterprises to optimize management configuration and improve ESG governance.
