title: Pengaruh Penghindaran Pajak, Kepemilikan Manajerial, dan Komite Audit terhadap Nilai Perusahaan
summary: This study aims to analyze the influence of tax avoidance, managerial ownership, and the audit committee on firm value for industrial sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the 2020–2024 period. The analytical method employed is multiple linear regression, incorporating both simultaneous and partial tests. The results indicate that, simultaneously, tax avoidance, managerial ownership, and the audit committee have a significant influence on firm value. This suggests that these three variables, when considered collectively, are relevant determinants in shaping investor perception of a company's value. However, the partial test results reveal that only managerial ownership has a significant effect on firm value, demonstrating that the alignment of interests between managers and shareholders through equity ownership is a mechanism positively responded to by the market. Conversely, tax avoidance and the audit committee, when examined individually, do not exert a significant influence on firm value within the industrial sector during the observed period. These findings provide insights for corporate management regarding the importance of ownership structure as a signal to investors, as well as the need to evaluate the effectiveness of other corporate governance policies in optimizing firm value.

title: Advanced Accounting Tools for Managing Costs and Financial Flows
summary: Purpose: This study quantifies the impact of intelligent accounting tools on enterprises' cost management and financial flows, focusing on medium and large enterprises in the manufacturing and service sectors. Research Limitation: The proposed methodology provides a basis for further research on the economic effects of accounting intellectualisation in different sectors and business environments. Findings: The results showed a statistically significant positive impact of the level of accounting intellectualisation on enterprises' operating profitability. The results also showed a statistically significant positive impact of the level of accounting intellectualisation on enterprises' operating profitability. These enterprises also had higher cash flow turnover. Quantitative estimates confirmed the economic significance of the effect even with a moderate increase in the level of accounting digitalisation. Practical Implication: The results can inform digital transformation strategies, assess the development level of accounting systems, and justify investments in enterprises' financial and analytical infrastructure. Social Implication: More efficient accounting systems support sustainable enterprise development by improving cost and financial flow management. summary: This study investigates the influence of Green Accounting, independent commissioners, and audit committees on firm value in Basic Materials companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2021–2024, with profitability included as a control variable. The study is motivated by the environmental challenges faced by the Basic Materials sector, particularly the increasing demand for sustainability practices and effective corporate governance to enhance firm value. This research employed a quantitative explanatory approach using secondary panel data obtained from annual reports, sustainability reports, and financial statements. Purposive sampling resulted in 53 companies, which were subsequently reduced to 43 companies with 172 firm-year observations after outlier treatment. Data were analyzed using panel data regression with the Fixed Effect Model selected through Chow and Hausman tests. The findings reveal that Green Accounting has a significant negative effect on firm value, indicating that investors tend to perceive environmental disclosure as a short-term cost burden rather than a long-term benefit. Meanwhile, independent commissioners, audit committees, and profitability do not significantly affect firm value. These findings extend Agency Theory by suggesting that the value relevance of environmental disclosure depends on industrial characteristics and investors’ time horizons.

title: BUXGALTERIYA HISOBI VA AUDIT JARAYONLARIGA SUN'IY INTELLEKT TEXNOLOGIYALARINI JORIY ETISHNING SAMARADORLIGI VA RIVOJLANISH ISTIQBOLLARI
summary: Maqolada Oʻzbekistonda buxgalteriya hisobi va audit jarayonlariga sun'iy intellekt texnologiyalarini joriy etishning samaradorligi va rivojlanish istiqbollari tadqiq etilgan. 2022–2024-yillar tahlili buxgalteriya hisobi, audit va soliq maslahati xizmatlari hajmi (yanvar–iyun) 354,1 mlrd soʻmdan 607,1 mlrd soʻmga, ya'ni 1,71 baravar, axborot va aloqa xizmatlari hajmi esa 1,92 baravar oshganini koʻrsatdi; bu hisob-tahlil jarayonlarini avtomatlashtirishga talabni shakllantirmoqda. Hisob sikli va audit bosqichlarida sun'iy intellektdan foydalanish yoʻnalishlari tizimlashtirilib, ularning kutilayotgan samaralari va tavakkalchiliklari baholangan. Qabul qilingan sun'iy intellekt texnologiyalarini 2030-yilgacha rivojlantirish strategiyasida buxgalteriya hisobi va audit uchun alohida moʻljallar mavjud emasligi koʻrsatilgan. Sun'iy intellektni hisob-audit faoliyatiga bosqichma-bosqich joriy etish modeli va uning samaradorlik koʻrsatkichlari tizimi taklif etilgan. EN The article examines the efficiency and development prospects of introducing artificial intelligence technologies into accounting and audit processes in Uzbekistan. An analysis of 2022–2024 shows that the volume of accounting, audit and tax consulting services (January–June) grew from 354.1 to 607.1 billion soums, or 1.71 times, and the volume of information and communication services 1.92 times, creating demand for the automation of accounting and analytical processes. Areas of AI application across the stages of the accounting cycle and audit are systematized, and their expected effects and risks are assessed. It is shown that the adopted AI technology development strategy to 2030 contains no specific targets for accounting and audit. A phased model for introducing AI into accounting and audit activities and a system of performance indicators are proposed. summary: Mazkur maqolada bank sektorida raqamli texnologiyalar, xususan, fintech (moliyaviy texnologiyalar) platformalari, raqamli toʻlov tizimlari va blokcheyn (blockchain) texnologiyasining joriy etilishi davlat moliyasi boshqaruvi va budjet intizomiga qanday ta'sir koʻrsatishi ilmiy asosda yoritiladi. Shuningdek, blokcheyn asosida toʻlovlar reyestrini yuritishning oʻzgarmas ma'lumotlar bazasi, markazlashmagan nazorat mexanizmlari va real vaqt rejimidagi kuzatuv kabi imkoniyatlari budjet intizomiga ta'sir koʻrsatishi mumkin boʻlgan omillar sifatida koʻrib chiqiladi. EN This article examines the impact of the introduction of digital technologies in the banking sector, particularly fintech platforms, digital payment systems, and blockchain technology, on public financial management and budget discipline. The study analyzes the role of fintech solutions in enhancing transparency and accountability in budgetary processes through faster payments, improved transaction security, and automated data recording. It also considers the use of blockchain-based payment registries, including immutable databases, decentralized control mechanisms, and real-time monitoring, as factors that may influence budget discipline. title: Determinan Kualitas Pelaporan Keuangan: Bukti Empiris pada Perusahaan Sektor Pertanian yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia Periode 2020–2022
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of audit quality, audit committee, firm size, and leverage on the quality of financial reporting in agricultural sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2020–2022 period. Financial reporting quality is proxied by accounting conservatism. This research employs a quantitative approach with a causal research design using secondary data obtained from the annual reports and financial statements of the sample companies. The sample consists of 24 agricultural companies selected through purposive sampling, resulting in a total of 60 firm-year observations. Data were analyzed using binary logistic regression with the assistance of EViews software. The findings indicate that audit quality, audit committee, firm size, and leverage do not have a statistically significant effect on financial reporting quality. These results suggest that the quality of financial reporting in agricultural companies has not been significantly influenced by the four variables examined. Therefore, financial reporting quality is likely to be affected by other factors, such as the effectiveness of internal controls, the implementation of good corporate governance, profitability, ownership structure, and earnings management practices. This study is expected to contribute to the accounting literature, particularly regarding the determinants of financial reporting quality in the agricultural sector, and to provide valuable insights for investors, auditors, corporate management, and regulators in enhancing financial reporting transparency and reliability.

title: Digital Transformation and ESG Synergy in Enhancing Enterprise Market Value
summary: Coordinating digital transformation with environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices is essential for corporate sustainability. Examining how this coordination affects enterprise market value clarifies the value implications of integrating the two strategies. Drawing on 26,486 firm–year observations for Chinese A-share firms during 2011–2024, this study constructs a digital transformation–ESG synergy (DESG) index using a coupling coordination degree (CCD) model that integrates annual-report digital transformation frequency and Huazheng ESG performance scores. A two-way fixed-effects model is used for estimation. The reported baseline shows a significant positive association between DESG and enterprise market value after controlling for firm characteristics and firm and year fixed effects. First-link mechanism analysis indicates that DESG is positively associated with firms’ internal conversion capacities (absorptive, innovation, and adaptive capabilities), operational green transformation, and external corporate reputation. Moderation analysis further shows that all five internal and external moderators positively shift the marginal DESG–market value slope: media coverage and green governance recognition amplify the positive association across all quartiles, whereas entrepreneurial spirit, new quality productive forces, and analyst attention exhibit threshold effects in which the marginal slope shifts from negative or null in the lowest quartile to significantly positive at the median and upper quartiles. Heterogeneity analysis further reveals that this association is more pronounced in eastern and central China and among high-technology, state-owned, and large firms. The findings provide firm-level evidence on the market value implications of digital–ESG synergy and offer theoretical and managerial implications for coordinating the two strategies.

title: The influence of FinTech adoption on sustainability performance: the mediating roles of financial inclusion and digital transformation
summary: Abstract This research aims to analyze how FinTech adoption (FA), mediated by digital transformation (DT) and financial inclusion (FI), influences sustainability performance (SP) in Jordan’s commercial banking sector. The study focuses on bank managers as participants because they play key roles in managing FA, DT, and SP. Study collected 395 questionnaire responses sufficient for analysis using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) in Smart PLS 4.0. The results showed that DT positively influences SP, suggesting that banks’ digital initiatives are important for advancing sustainable business practices. The study confirms that FA significantly drives both DT and FI. This indicates that integrating financial technologies improves banking services and supports the digital transformation of banking operations. The study confirms that FA directly and positively determines a bank’s SP. Moreover, the study highlights significant mediation, showing that both FI and DT positively affect banks’ SP and validating multiple pathways through which FinTech supports sustainable outcomes. The results also show that FA and FI cross multiple dimensions, enhance an institution’s SP, which is particularly relevant to managers and policymakers seeking to advance sustainable development through digital finance innovations.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND VALUE CREATION IN BROILER PRODUCTION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW ON ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND FRUGAL INNOVATION
summary: This article analyzes how digital solutions applied to environmental monitoring contribute to value creation in broiler production, through the lens of frugal innovation.The study departs from the observation that sensors, the Internet of Things (IoT), automation, predictive models, and decision support systems expand the collection and interpretation of environmental data, but do not always demonstrate economic, productive, operational, or socio-environmental value under real production conditions.A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, in the Scopus and Web of Science databases, covering publications from 2020 to 2026.After the selection process, 73 articles comprised the taxonomic synthesis.The results indicate that value creation appears most consistently in the informational, operational, and decision-making dimensions, while economic and productive effects remain underreported.Frugality was associated with the use of low-cost sensors, microcontrollers, open-source software, mobile applications, and modular architectures.The article contributes by connecting production constraints, digital solutions, technological functions, frugal innovation, value creation, and adherence to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 2, 9, 12, and 13).

title: The Impact of Cross-Border Data Regulation on the Resilience of China’s Industrial and Supply Chains
summary: Digital transformation has created huge economic benefits for cross-border data flow around the world, but it has also caused real problems such as violating privacy and leaking business secrets. For China, how to manage data well and maintain the stability of the industrial supply chain is a difficult policy problem in the negotiation of international rules. This article analyzes two opposite effects of cross-border data regulation. On the one hand, strict regulatory review and uncertain policy results will increase the compliance burden of enterprises. This will lead to the interruption of information exchange in the supply chain, which will weaken the ability of the supply chain to recover from the shock. On the other hand, if the regulatory framework is stable and predictable, mutual trust can be established between enterprises, which will help improve the adaptability of the supply chain. Whether regulatory rules are beneficial to the supply chain or harmful to the supply chain depends on two practical conditions: first, whether domestic rules are in line with international norms, and second, the degree of dependence of the industry on data resources. Combined with the experience of the three-stage reform of China's data outbound management and the actual cases of logistics and digital trade industries, this article believes that policymakers should no longer be entangled in the simple debate of "should be relaxed or tight" the rules, but should focus on establishing institutional interoperability. Specifically, a practical balance between data supervision and supply chain resilience can be found by unifying negative lists, promoting mutual recognition of regulators, and introducing business continuity assessment tools.

title: Audit Committee Diligence and Financial Reporting Quality of listed Non-Financial Firms in Sub-Saharan Africa
summary: The study aims to address the inconsistency and unreliability of financial Reports among listed firms in Sub-Saharan Africa, attributed to insufficient audit committee diligence, lack of expertise, and limited oversight resources. By examining the impact of audit committee diligence on financial Reporting quality, the study seeks to enhance understanding of corporate governance mechanisms in the unique context of Sub-Saharan Africa. The main finding highlights the significant positive effect of audit committee diligence on financial Reporting quality. The study employed a panel dynamic regression analysis, using secondary data sourced from annual Reports of 235 non-financial firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group, Johannesburg Stock Exchange, and Nairobi Stock Exchange from 2013 to 2022. The Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) regression model was utilized to account for endogeneity and heteroscedasticity issues, ensuring robust and reliable results. The analysis reveals that audit committee diligence, particularly the frequency and effectiveness of meetings, significantly enhances the quality of financial Reporting. The results indicate a positive relationship between the number of audit committee meetings and financial Reporting quality, as measured by Jones Discretionary Accrual, with a significant coefficient (0.041, p < 0.05). This underscores the crucial role of diligent audit committees in improving financial transparency and reliability. This study contributes to the existing literature by providing empirical evidence on the importance of audit committee diligence in the context of SubSaharan Africa, a region that has been largely overlooked in previous research. The findings offer valuable insights for policymakers, regulators, and stakeholders, emphasizing the need for robust governance mechanisms to enhance financial Reporting quality and foster economic growth. The study also lays the groundwork for future research to explore other dimensions of audit committee effectiveness.

title: Extreme Climate Events, Governance Deficits, and Adaptation Failure in Africa: A Policy and Framework Review
summary: Africa accounts for less than four per cent of cumulative global greenhouse gas emissions, yet it absorbs some of the most severe consequences of anthropogenic climate change. The literature documenting this disparity has grown substantially over the past decade, but most reviews stop at cataloguing impacts and listing recommendations. This paper goes further. Drawing on a PRISMA 2020-compliant review of 79 peer-reviewed studies and verified institutional reports published between 2019 and 2025, we develop the Africa Climate Resilience and Justice Framework (ACRJF): a four-domain policy architecture designed to address the structural deficits that cause climate adaptation to fail in African contexts. The four domains are the science-policy interface, sectoral adaptation governance, climate finance architecture, and intersectional vulnerability reduction. The framework is grounded in the evidence, not imposed on it: each domain responds directly to a pattern of failure identified across the literature. The paper also applies the framework to all five African sub-regions, showing how domain priorities shift with hazard profile and institutional context. Eight critical evidence and governance gaps are identified. The central argument is that climate resilience in Africa will not be achieved by more knowledge alone, but by institutional reform, redistributive finance, and governance that takes seriously both the evidence and the communities most exposed to harm.

title: Board monitoring and the informational content of ESG performance
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine whether improvements in environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance are associated with subsequent realised firm outcomes and whether board monitoring conditions these relationships. Using UK FTSE 350 firms, the study evaluates whether year-on-year ESG improvements predict ESG controversies, environmental incidents, investment inefficiency and future operating performance. It further investigates whether stronger board monitoring increases the extent to which ESG improvements are associated with favourable subsequent outcomes. Design/methodology/approach The study uses an unbalanced panel of 314 FTSE 350 firms, comprising 4,396 firm-year observations from 2010 to 2024, with ESG, governance and financial data from LSEG. Panel regressions include industry and year fixed effects with firm-clustered standard errors. Board monitoring is measured using a composite index based on board independence, CEO-chair role separation and board ESG expertise. Robustness tests include disaggregated governance components, an ESG measure excluding the governance pillar, firm fixed effects, lagged specifications and multicollinearity diagnostics. Findings ESG improvements are not consistently associated with subsequent ESG controversies, investment inefficiency or future operating performance. For environmental incidents, however, the interaction between ESG improvement and board monitoring is negative and statistically significant, indicating that the association becomes more favourable as monitoring strengthens. Component-level analyses show similar negative moderation for board independence, CEO-chair separation and ESG expertise, although statistical strength varies. The result also remains when the governance pillar is excluded from the ESG measure. Lagged specifications provide more limited evidence, indicating that the relationship is outcome-specific and not persistent across all time horizons. Research limitations/implications The study focuses on UK listed firms operating within a relatively strong governance environment, which may limit generalisability to weaker institutional settings. The board monitoring index uses equal weighting, although component-level tests reduce concerns regarding this construction. The outcome measures capture specific dimensions of realised firm behaviour and do not directly measure greenwashing, managerial intent or board detection processes. Future research could examine alternative governance measures, weighting schemes, outcome intensity, other institutional settings and additional mechanisms such as ownership structure, executive incentives and external assurance. Practical implications The findings suggest that ESG score improvements should not be interpreted in isolation as evidence of substantive operational change. For boards, the results highlight the importance of effective oversight in linking ESG initiatives to underlying business practices, particularly in environmentally sensitive areas. For investors, ESG changes may be more informative when considered alongside governance characteristics. For regulators and standard setters, the evidence suggests that enhanced ESG disclosure alone may be insufficient unless supported by governance structures that promote accountability and substantive implementation. Social implications The study has broader implications for corporate accountability and stakeholder confidence in ESG information. By showing that ESG improvements are not uniformly associated with realised outcomes, the findings reinforce the need for stronger governance and scrutiny over how sustainability claims relate to actual corporate behaviour. More credible alignment between ESG performance and operational conduct may improve the usefulness of sustainability information for employees, communities, investors and other stakeholders and may help reduce the risk that symbolic improvements are interpreted as evidence of substantive social or environmental progress. Originality/value The study contributes by shifting attention from ESG levels to the informational content of ESG improvements and their association with subsequent realised outcomes. It further shows that this relationship is conditional on board monitoring and differs across outcome types. Unlike studies focused mainly on ESG disclosure or contemporaneous firm value, this study links changes in ESG performance to future adverse events, investment efficiency and operating performance. It also provides new evidence that the environmental-outcome relationship is not solely driven by the construction of the composite monitoring index or mechanical overlap with the ESG governance pillar.

title: Green Entrepreneurship sebagai Strategi Hilirisasi Produk Kayu Berkelanjutan: Studi Konseptual pada Pengembangan Engineered Wood Product (EWP) di PT Jaya Cemerlang Industry
summary: The transition toward a green economy, the Net Zero Emission (NZE) target, and the growing market demand for legal, sustainable, and traceable wood products have encouraged Indonesia's forestry industry to develop sustainability-oriented innovations. One of these innovations is Engineered Wood Products (EWP), which utilize fast-growing timber to produce high value-added products. Although research on green entrepreneurship has expanded considerably, studies integrating green entrepreneurship, green innovation, green branding, forestry downstreaming, and the Timber Legality and Sustainability Verification System (SVLK) in the development of EWP in Indonesia remain limited. This study aims to analyze the implementation of green entrepreneurship in the development of "Kayu Pintar" as a sustainable forestry downstreaming strategy. The study employs a qualitative descriptive approach using the library research method. Data were collected from reputable scientific publications, government documents, and industry publications as implementation illustrations, and were analyzed using content analysis. The findings indicate that EWP development enhances the value of fast-growing timber, improves raw material utilization efficiency, and reduces pressure on natural forests. Furthermore, the implementation of SVLK and green branding strategies strengthens product legality, sustainability, and competitiveness. The integration of green entrepreneurship, green innovation, green branding, and SVLK contributes to improving the competitiveness and export performance of Indonesia's forestry products.

title: Operational strategies for managing purchase decisions in festival shopping: Analyzing the role of fear of missing out (FOMO) in the digital transformation era
summary: Purpose: For most consumers who experience fear of missing out, regret related to falling behind trends outweighs regret related to financial costs. In fact, the intensity of the attraction created through fear of missing out is positively correlated with impulse buying, which potentially reduces self-control during shopping activities. Hence, fear of missing out is considered a psychological disorder that affects the mental health of the individual. Therefore, this study aims to explain the reactive-behavioral outcomes (e.g., impulsive buying decisions) by emphasizing the perceptual drivers of the 'Fear Of Missing Out' (FOMO) phenomenon within the context of festival shopping opportunities in the digital transformation era.Methodology: This study is a basic-applied research based on its purpose and a mixed research based on its research strategy. The qualitative strategy used in the first stage of the research is grounded theory and the quantitative strategies used in this survey-correlational research. The qualitative participants included marketing and sales consultants as well as professors of business, marketing, and e-commerce, 10 of whom were selected as participants through non-probability judgmental sampling. The statistical population of the quantitative part of the study is people who visited various festivals and made various purchases.The sampling method in the quantitative section was random, and the sample size was determined to be 221 participants based on relationship of Cohen. To prevent sample attrition, about 240 questionnaires were distributed in this study and 229 questionnaires were returned to the researcher.Findings: The results showed that perceptual drivers (positive customer perception of the brand, deceptive advertising, customer experience, and customer emotional intelligence) lead to strengthening the fear of missing out on festival shopping opportunities. Also, the pivotal phenomenon (fear of missing out on festival shopping opportunities), individual-marketing factors, and technological factors lead to strengthening customer acumen (smart and responsible shopping, strengthening the buyer's financial knowledge and awareness, and managing market rumors). Finally, it was determined that customer intelligence (smart and responsible shopping, strengthening the buyer's financial knowledge and awareness, and managing market rumors) leads to a reduction in undesirable behavioral-reactive outcomes and a strengthening of desirable behavioral-reactive outcomes.Originality/Value: According to the results obtained from the implementation of the qualitative and quantitative parts of the research, the variables 1) deceptive advertising, 2) customer emotional intelligence, 3) customer respect for the brand, 4) buyer confusion, 5) brand uniqueness, 6) brand community, 7) brand love, 8) brand attachment, 9) customer thirst for shopping, 10) market rumor management, 11) digital age, 12) negative internal emotions, 13) customer mental anxiety, 14) interaction-communication problems, and 15) customer resentment, 16) brand responsibility are considered new research findings.

title: Efektivitas Penerapan Green Accounting dalam Pengelolaan Limbah Industri Kelapa Sawit: Studi Kasus pada PT Putra Bangka Mandiri
summary: The palm oil industry generates significant waste, requiring integrated Green Accounting. This study analyzes Green Accounting implementation in palm oil waste management at PT Putra Bangka Mandiri across five stages, namely identification, recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure, evaluates the effectiveness of its Zero Waste program based on four operational dimensions (perceived benefits, stakeholder access to benefits, implementation consistency, and information traceability), and identifies the barriers and supporting factors involved. A descriptive qualitative approach with a single case study method was used. Data were collected via interviews with eleven informants, document review, and field observation, analyzed thematically through data reduction, display, and conclusion drawing. Results show Green Accounting implementation remains partial: identification and measurement have been carried out, but environmental costs are still recorded with general operating costs rather than separately. The Zero Waste program is assessed as relatively effective in managing POME based on these dimensions, but distribution of fruit bunches to partner farmers remains uneven due to stock, queue, quota, and transport-cost constraints. Other barriers include fire risk from solid waste stockpiles and weak integration between operational and accounting data. The study concludes that effective environmental management requires stronger linkage among physical data, costs, accounting information, and stakeholder benefits.

title: Prioritizing and selecting the G-resilient suppliers in the natural stone industry using a hybrid multi-criteria decision-making approach: BWM-TRUST
summary: Purpose: In today's turbulent and uncertain environment, organizations are compelled to revise traditional supply chain approaches and adopt strategies that simultaneously address environmental sustainability and resilience to disruptions. Accordingly, this study aims to develop a decision-making framework for evaluating and selecting green-resilient suppliers in the natural stone industry—suppliers that demonstrate both strong environmental performance and the ability to respond quickly and effectively to disruptions. Methodology: This research employs a hybrid Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) framework that integrates the Best-Worst Method (BWM) to determine the weights of evaluation criteria with the mulTi-noRmalization mUltiDistance aSsessmenT (TRUST) technique to rank suppliers as alternatives. The evaluation criteria, categorized into "green" and "resilience" dimensions, were identified through a comprehensive literature review and expert input. These criteria include: waste generation, employee training, possession of eco-friendly certifications, pollution control initiatives, responsiveness, coordination, agility, information sharing, and efficient resource utilization. Data related to five real suppliers in the natural stone industry were collected through expert surveys and fed into the proposed evaluation model. Findings: The results revealed that "efficient resource utilization" holds the highest weight among the green and resilience criteria. Furthermore, based on the TRUST-based ranking, supplier A2 was identified as the top-performing green-resilient supplier. Originality/Value: The proposed model offers a practical, structured tool to help supply chain managers enhance sustainability and resilience amid growing environmental and operational disruptions.

title: The Impact of Business Environmental Changes on the Adoption of a Strategic Pivot: A Case Study of Zar Industrial Group
summary: Objective: This study aimed to examine the impact of business environmental changes on strategic pivot adoption in Zar Industrial Group and develop a conceptual model of this process. Methods and Materials: This applied qualitative study used a grounded theory design. The study population consisted of Zar Industrial Group managers and university professors with expertise in strategic management and organizational change. Participants were selected purposively based on their knowledge and professional experience. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with managers of the holding company and its food-industry subsidiaries, together with academic experts. Interviews continued until theoretical saturation, resulting in a final sample of 12 participants. Interview transcripts were systematically coded, compared, and categorized to identify the principal dimensions and mechanisms associated with strategic pivot adoption. Findings: The analysis produced seven main categories and 41 related concepts. The categories included macro-environmental changes and external pressures; risk, uncertainty, and financial pressure; supply-chain and operational disruptions; market-oriented and commercial responses; structural and business-model redesign; innovation, technology, and digital transformation; and human capital, organizational learning, and institutionalization of the strategic pivot. Environmental turbulence generated financial, operational, and market pressures that stimulated coordinated strategic responses. These responses involved market reorientation, business-model redesign, technological innovation, digital transformation, and capability development. Human capital and organizational learning played a central role in sustaining and institutionalizing the strategic pivot. Conclusion: Strategic pivot adoption in Zar Industrial Group represents a multidimensional organizational response to environmental uncertainty rather than an isolated managerial decision. Successful pivots require alignment among market responses, structural transformation, technological innovation, operational resilience, and organizational learning. The proposed conceptual model can help managers recognize environmental signals, coordinate adaptive actions, and strengthen organizational resilience and long-term competitiveness.

title: The Role of Corporate Governance in Promoting Accountability and Transparency in Companies in Uganda
summary: Corporate governance connects the exercise of company powers with the obligation to explain decisions, disclose material interests and account for corporate resources. This article examines its role in promoting accountability and transparency in Ugandan companies through a doctrinal and documentary review. It analyses the Companies Act, Cap 106, sector specific legislation and ten judicial decisions, comprising four Ugandan and six comparative common law authorities. Academic literature supplies the conceptual basis for examining board oversight, stakeholder interests, information and internal controls. The analysis finds that governance depends on more than incorporation, formal resolutions or published codes. Effective accountability requires identifiable duties, reliable transaction records, management of conflicts, access to an appropriate forum and a legally available remedy. Ugandan decisions demonstrate both the limits of using corporate personality to conceal wrongdoing and the importance of correct parties and procedure. Comparative decisions clarify unauthorised profits, secret commissions, proper purpose and creditor interests during financial distress. The article recommends proportionate governance arrangements, transaction specific conflict procedures, documented board reasoning, protected reporting routes and consistent follow up of audit findings. It does not report a new survey or measure a causal effect of governance on company performance. Its contribution is a legally grounded account of how information and oversight become enforceable responsibility in Uganda.

title: Governing Digital Transformation for Climate Resilience and Circular Economy: Institutional Capacity, Indigenous Inclusion, and Sustainable Development in Chittagong Hill Tracts, Evidence from Bandarban, Bangladesh
summary: Abstract Digital transformation is often presented as a means of improving public service delivery, climate-risk communication, environmental monitoring, and resource efficiency. Its contribution to resilience and sustainability, however, depends on institutional capacity, accessible infrastructure, inclusive decision-making, and accountable data governance. This study examines how these conditions shape digital governance for climate resilience and circular-economy development in Bandarban, Bangladesh. Using a qualitative case-study design, the study draws on four focus group discussions (FGDs) and 20 key informant interviews (KIIs), analysed thematically through the Institutional-Capacity and Inclusive Digital Resilience Framework (ICIDRF). The analysis identifies five interconnected themes: weak digital infrastructure; institutional coordination gaps; affordability and digital-skills constraints; gaps in climate-information and public-service delivery; and barriers to Indigenous-language access and representation. Together, these themes indicate that digital tools cannot deliver inclusive outcomes in isolation. Their effectiveness depends on reliable connectivity and maintenance, clear institutional responsibilities, communication channels that communities can access and understand, and meaningful Indigenous participation in the design and governance of services. The analysis also highlights the need to connect digital systems to locally feasible climate-adaptation and circular-economy practices rather than treating technology as an end in itself. The study contributes an inclusion-centred framework for understanding digital transformation in a geographically remote and culturally diverse setting. It recommends strengthening cross-agency coordination, providing multilingual and offline communication options, protecting Indigenous knowledge and community data, and evaluating initiatives against practical social, environmental, and governance outcomes. The findings offer context-specific insights for more accountable and inclusive sustainable-development policy in Bandarban and comparable regions.

title: Generative Al Adoption and Marketing Performance in Digital Finance: The Mediating Role of Digital Product Innovation
summary: This study examines the relationship between Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption and marketing performance in digital finance, focusing on the mediating role of digital product innovation. The study aims to explain how AI adoption can support marketing effectiveness by facilitating the development of innovative digital financial products and services. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was proposed, with primary data intended to be collected through a structured, self-administered questionnaire distributed via Google Forms to a target sample of 335 respondents working in banks, FinTech companies, and digital financial institutions in Pakistan, including HBL, UBL, National Bank of Pakistan, Allied Bank, Bank Alfalah, JazzCash, and Easypaisa. Convenience sampling was proposed to recruit respondents familiar with digital finance, marketing, and AI-supported activities. The planned statistical analysis included demographic frequencies and percentages, Cronbach’s alpha reliability analysis, Pearson correlation, linear regression, and mediation analysis using PROCESS Macro Model 4 with 5,000 bootstrap samples and 95% confidence intervals. The illustrative results indicated a positive relationship between Generative AI adoption and marketing performance (\(r = .624, p < .001\)) and a positive association between Generative AI adoption and digital product innovation (\(r = .587, p < .01\)). The proposed mediation analysis further suggested a positive indirect relationship between Generative AI adoption and marketing performance through digital product innovation (\(\beta = .247\), 95% bootstrap confidence interval \([.160, .345]\)). These potential findings emphasize that the value of Generative AI may extend beyond technology adoption to the development of innovative, customer-oriented financial products that strengthen marketing activities. The study offers practical implications for banks and FinTech organizations seeking to enhance customer engagement, improve digital service development, and strengthen their competitive position through responsible AI integration. It also provides a foundation for future research examining AI-driven innovation and marketing outcomes in emerging digital financial markets. The statistical values are illustrative rather than calculated from actual respondent data and must be replaced with verified empirical results before the abstract is used as a report of completed research.

title: The 3B-SMITR Framework A Framework for Environmental State and Environmental Management
summary: Environmental management systems frequently collect large quantities of data while failing to establish clear links between environmental observations and management actions. Conversely, management plans often prescribe interventions without explicit connections to measurable environmental conditions. The 3B-SMITR Framework addresses this challenge by separating environmental condition from environmental governance. The 3B Framework describes environmental state through the concepts of Background, Baseline and Benchmark. The SMITR Framework describes environmental management through the concepts of Sensor, Metric, Indicator, Threshold and Response. The 3B Framework answers the question: What condition is the environment in? The SMITR Framework answers the question: How do we observe, evaluate and respond to that condition? The two frameworks intersect through the Benchmark, which defines the desired environmental condition against which performance is assessed and management interventions are triggered. The framework is intended for application in mine closure, water stewardship, environmental compliance, ecological rehabilitation, adaptive management and environmental digital twins.

title: Buy Now and Pay Later in Emerging Markets: Exploring Why customers Adopt the Service
summary: Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) services are expanding rapidly in emerging markets, yet limited research has examined the consumer factors shaping their adoption in Saudi Arabia. This study investigates the influence of trust, electronic word of mouth (eWOM), and attitude toward cash on delivery (COD) on consumers’ intention to adopt BNPL services, drawing on the Theory of Planned Behavior. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from 300 respondents, including both users and non-users of BNPL services. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis were used to assess the measurement model, and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) was applied to test the proposed relationships among the latent constructs. The results show that trust and eWOM effects BNPL adoption positively, while attitude toward COD has a negative effect. The findings suggest that consumer trust and online recommendations shape BNPL adoption, whereas preference for COD reduce consumers’ willingness to use BNPL services. The study offers implications for FinTech providers, retailers, and regulators in emerging markets.

summary: Technological advancements that have made access easier for all users have increased social media usage among Generation Z, which in turn has fueled a “Fear of Missing Out” (FOMO) mentality and consumerist behavior. A lack of self-control and knowledge leads students to make impulsive purchases and lack an understanding of wise financial management. Therefore, financial literacy education was provided through Community Service using the Service Learning method, implemented for students in class X2 at Petra 3 Christian High School Surabaya so that students would gain an understanding of financial literacy from an early age. The Service Learning activity was carried out in three stages: preparation, implementation, and evaluation. The material was delivered through presentations, followed by discussions and a mini-quiz using the Wayground interactive platform, with the aim of making the activity interactive and increasing student participation throughout the session. The material covered the definition, impacts, causes, and ways to address consumerist attitudes, followed by an introduction to the basics of capital market investment instruments, namely stock and mutual fund investments. The results of the Service Learning activity indicated students’ enthusiasm, as reflected in their participation in answering questions during the interactive mini-quiz on Wayground. Their correct answers also suggested an understanding of consumer behavior and the fundamentals of stock and mutual fund investments.

title: Islamic corporate social responsibility as a governance-embedded system: evidence from Islamic banks in Malaysia and Indonesia
summary: Purpose Although there has been a rapid rate of expansion observed in the domain of Islamic banking, there remains an inconsistent degree of institutionalisation of Islamic corporate social responsibility (ICSR). The reason is that a higher priority level has been placed on contractual and financial compliance by existing CSR and Shariah governance models, rather than broader socio-economic aspects. The purpose of this study was to develop an ICSR framework to assess the capacity of existing Islamic banking institutions to institutionalise ICSR through relevant governance mechanisms and Islamic social finance instruments, while examining their relationships with socio-economic outcomes. Design/methodology/approach In this investigation, a qualitative multiple-case study design, which involved both Maybank Islamic (Malaysia) and Bank Syariah Indonesia (Indonesia), was employed. Specifically, semi-structured interviews were conducted with a total of 20 purposively selected senior informants, with 10 from each of the two institutions, who were directly involved in the process of ICSR governance and implementation. The interviews, which ranged between 60 and 120 min, were triangulated with corresponding institutional and sustainability documents. After collecting the data, a thematic content analysis was performed through the NVivo software, which incorporated iterative coding, intercoder verification, participant validation and cross-case comparison to identify relevant patterns of ICSR institutionalisation and socio-economic value creation. Findings The findings revealed a clear hierarchy of ICSR institutionalisation, wherein zakat represented the most formally embedded instrument, supported by Shariah oversight, structured procedures, auditing and reporting. Meanwhile, voluntary instruments, including sadaqah and infaq, and developmental instruments, such as qard al-hasan and waqf, exhibited weaker and more fragmented degrees of organisational integration. Four differentiated socio-economic outcome clusters were associated with the above instruments, namely, immediate relief and redistribution (zakat), community trust and relational legitimacy (sadaqah or infaq), economic empowerment (qard al-hasan) and long-term or intergenerational welfare (waqf). Importantly, the interview results demonstrated an institutionalisation–impact paradox, in which instruments associated with greater long-term developmental potential were not equivalent to those most strongly embedded within existing structures of governance. Practical implications A policy-relevant framework was provided for existing Islamic banking institutions, regulators and Shariah boards to strengthen the governance, coordination, measurement and reporting aspects of relevant ICSR instruments that were often under-institutionalised. The proposed framework could also inform the development of Shariah-specific social responsibility indicators that were aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which could enable more substantive and comparable assessment of ICSR beyond conventional CSR reporting processes. Originality/value Islamic ethical underpinnings, Shariah governance structures, Islamic social finance tools and various socio-economic outcomes were incorporated in this study into a consolidated and empirically grounded framework. Particularly, it was demonstrated that there were varying levels of institutionalisation and socio-economic value observed in existing ICSR instruments, which highlighted the existence of an institutionalisation–impact paradox. As such, there was a deeper understanding of how Islamic obligations are converted from religious teachings into actual organisational practice and developmental value.

title: Enabling artificial intelligence in entrepreneurship: Implications for startup creation in higher education
summary: The digital transformation has reshaped entrepreneurship, with the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) as a powerful enabler of innovation and startup creation. However, higher education institutions face challenges integrating AI into entrepreneurship education curriculum, limiting students’ ability to fully harness its potential. This study aimed to determine and explore entrepreneurship students’ challenges in using AI for startup development, assess the competencies they gain in innovating business ideas, and analyze how these challenges affect competencies using structural equation modeling (SEM). Employing an convergent mixed-method design, the study surveyed 114 third- and fourth-year BS Entrepreneurship students and conducted interviews to faculty and business plan implementers. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and SEM, while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis for triangulation. Findings revealed that students face significant challenges in opportunity identification, decision-making, performance execution, education and learning, and research application. The key barriers highlight was market understanding, lack of AI literacy, limited mentorship, and insufficient curriculum integration. Despite these, students reported gaining competencies in opportunity recognition, customer targeting, data-informed decision-making, and entrepreneurial communication using AI tools. However, critical thinking, problem-solving, and prototyping skills remained underdeveloped. SEM results indicated that challenges in education, opportunity identification, and decision-making significantly constrained entrepreneurial competencies. The study implies the need for higher education to reform curricula by embedding AI-focused modules, case-based projects, mentorship opportunities, and innovation hubs. Strengthening AI-driven entrepreneurship education will equip students with the competencies required for sustainable startup creation in the digital economy.

title: Implementation of a Web-Based Sales Information System for Culinary MSMEs: A Case Study of Bakmi Jogja and Mie Ayam Bangka
summary: Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) play a vital role in the local economy, yet many still rely on manual recording of sales transactions and financial reports, increasing the risk of calculation errors and delaying report preparation. This operational constraint was identified at Bakmi Jogja and Mie Ayam Bangka, a culinary MSME outlet in Cipinang Besar Selatan, East Jakarta, that offers two flagship menu lines within a single business establishment. This study aimed to design, implement, and evaluate a web-based sales information system to address these operational challenges. A descriptive qualitative case-study method was applied, with empirical data gathered through interviews, direct observation, and literature review. System development followed the Prototype model comprising communication, quick planning, modeling, prototype construction, and deployment with user feedback. The system was developed using the CodeIgniter 4 framework, a MySQL/MariaDB database, and the Midtrans payment gateway for QRIS-based digital payments, followed by deployment on commercial cloud hosting for actual operational adoption rather than offline simulation. Black box testing evaluating authentication, product management, transaction recording, payment integration, order-status tracking, promotional banner management, and financial reporting yielded valid results across all twelve test scenarios spanning seven functional modules. As early empirical evidence, the system logged five operational transactions over a seven-day observation window, four of which were completed with confirmed revenue of IDR 224,000, identifying Bakmi Jogja Godog Special as the top-selling menu item. These findings demonstrate that the system transitioned manual record-keeping to automated, database-backed transactions, accelerated financial report generation from approximately one week to an on-demand summary, and provided a digital storefront facilitating online ordering and marketing for the enterprise.

title: A Critical Review of Corporate Social Responsibility in African Manufacturing Sector: Revisioning of Future Research
summary: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) has become a central concept within the of sustainable development globally, yet its manifestation within the African manufacturing sector remains under-theorized and empirically fragmented. This paper critically reviews the current state of CSR research focusing on African manufacturing industries. Synthesizing literature from the past decade alongside seminal foundational works, this review maps the intellectual terrain of the field. The analysis reveals a pronounced geographic bias, with scholarship disproportionately concentrated on South Africa and Nigeria, leaving vast regions of the continent underrepresented. Furthermore, a significant sectoral gap exists; while extractive industries (oil and mining) are well-documented, heavy manufacturing sectors, such as aluminium processing, are notably absent from the discourse. Methodologically, the field suffers from an over-reliance on cross-sectional quantitative surveys and a lack of qualitative depth, limiting the understanding of contextual nuances. This paper contributes to the literature by the appraisal of the Western-centric theoretical frameworks often applied to African contexts and proposes a robust research agenda. The finding of this paper calls for sector-specific investigations, the adoption of indigenous theoretical lenses such as Ubuntu, and methodological diversification to better capture the complexities of CSR in the Global South.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL CONSTITUTIONALISM IN CRIMINAL LAW ENFORCEMENT OF FOREST FIRE CASES IN RIAU PROVINCE
summary: This study analyzes the enforcement of criminal law in forest fire cases in Riau Province from the perspective of environmental constitutionalism, which positions environmental protection as a constitutional right of citizens and a responsibility of the state. The research is motivated by the recurring forest and land fires that have caused serious impacts on public health, environmental sustainability, and socio-economic conditions, while environmental criminal law enforcement remains insufficient and ineffective. The study employs normative legal research using statutory, conceptual, and case approaches. Primary and secondary legal materials, as well as policy documents related to environmental law enforcement, were systematically examined. NVivo 12 Plus was used to support qualitative analysis and strengthen the interpretation of legal findings. The results show that Indonesia’s environmental criminal law framework is relatively adequate at the normative level; however, its implementation in handling forest fires in Riau continues to face structural challenges. These include inconsistent law enforcement, limited capacity and integrity of law enforcement officials, and weak corporate accountability in land management practices. Law enforcement tends to be reactive and focuses primarily on individual perpetrators rather than addressing corporate responsibility and broader structural causes. As a result, the constitutional mandate to guarantee the right to a good and healthy environment has not been fully realized. This study concludes that effective criminal law enforcement against forest fires requires the integration of constitutional principles, environmental policies, and fair law enforcement practices. Strengthening environmental constitutionalism is essential to ensure sustainable environmental governance and substantive protection of environmental rights.

title: Governance Configurations and Corporate Green Innovation: A Configurational Analysis
summary: ABSTRACT Green innovation has become a strategic choice for firms responding to environmental regulation and seeking competitive advantage. Prior research has focused primarily on the independent effects of internal and external governance elements, yet how these elements combine into configurations remains underexplored. Drawing on stakeholder theory, this study adopts a configurational perspective and employs fuzzy‐set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) to examine how internal and external governance elements jointly shape green innovation. The findings reveal three pathways: externally‐driven, internally‐driven, and synergistic balanced. No single governance element is necessary for high green innovation. The relationship among external governance elements depends on internal governance strength. When internal governance is limited, government subsidies, green investors, and supply chain finance operate synergistically. When internal governance is strong, government support and market capital become substitutable. The relationship among internal governance elements depends on the dominant resource source. When internal resources dominate, shareholder balance, executive compensation intensity, and technical directors reinforce one another. When external resources dominate, technical directors and executive compensation intensity appear in mutually exclusive configurations. These findings suggest that effective governance depends on coherence among selected elements rather than comprehensiveness across all dimensions. The study extends the stakeholder theory tradition on prioritization and trade‐offs by identifying the configurational conditions under which governance elements operate in synergy, substitution, or mutual exclusivity, offering a configurational lens for understanding corporate green innovation governance.

title: From Green Digital Transformation to Hotel Performance: The Roles of Dynamic Capabilities, Innovation Capabilities, and Organizational Resilience
summary: The hotel industry has acknowledged the growing environmental concern and recognized the significance of adopting sustainable practices. The existing literature on the hotel industry reflects a discernible gap between green digital transformation and green dynamic capabilities, green innovation capabilities, and organizational resilience. Therefore, this study aims to examine the relationships between green digital transformation, green dynamic capabilities, green innovation capabilities, organizational resilience, and organizational performance. Using purposive sampling, data were gathered from 329 managers working in four Chinese cities and analyzed through partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings highlight the significant positive association between green digital transformation, green dynamic capabilities and green innovation capabilities, which, in turn, are positively associated with hotel resilience. Furthermore, organizational resilience is significantly associated with process innovation, service innovation, and organizational performance. Practically, the study’s findings help encourage hotel managers to implement digital technologies to improve hotels’ efficiency and organizational performance. Moreover, the study encourages regulatory authorities to support green digitalization initiatives and improve hotels’ performances.

title: The impact of corporate social responsibility on inventory management: empirical evidence from China’s A-sector enterprises
summary: Purpose The significance of corporate social responsibility (CSR) in business operations has increasingly been recognized, with research indicating that socially responsible initiatives can improve multiple facets of firm performance. However, the impact of CSR on inventory management, a critical component of operational efficiency, remains underexplored. This study aims to investigate the influence of CSR on inventory management. Design/methodology/approach The analysis is based on 8,385 firm-year observations from 645 Chinese A-type listed companies from 2010 to 2022. The study employs fixed-effect, panel EGLS and system GMM models to ensure the results robustness. Findings The study finds that CSR positively influences inventory management, as firms with higher CSR engagement achieve better inventory turnover ratios. In addition, asset tangibility, firm size and firm efficiency contribute to improved inventory management. Practical implications Corporate managers should integrate CSR into core business strategies to enhance inventory management and overall operational efficiency. CSR-driven firms can achieve better inventory turnover while contributing to social and environmental goals, reinforcing the business case for responsible practices. title: R&D Investment and Corporate Sustainability Evidence from ICT Firms Listed in Korean Capital Markets
summary: This study examines the association between R&D expenditure, an input-based proxy for technological innovation activity (TIA), and ESG ratings among Korean listed ICT firms. The full sample comprises 501 firm-year observations from 122 firms over 2012–2024. A parsimonious pooled OLS analysis relates current ESG to TIA lagged by one calendar year, using 350 observations from 97 firms over 2013–2024. Lagged TIA is positively associated with overall ESG (coefficient = 0.2324; firm-clustered p = 0.0283). Dimension-specific coefficients are also positive, with Governance significant at the 5% level and Environmental and Social ratings at the 10% level under firm-clustered inference. Winsorizing lagged TIA at the 1st and 99th percentiles yields similar results. Contemporaneous OLS, exploratory quantile, and ordered logistic analyses provide supplementary evidence under different specifications. The principal estimates describe unadjusted associations and do not establish causality. The findings describe sector-specific relationships between innovation inputs and corporate sustainability rather than demonstrated innovation outcomes or sustainability mechanisms.

title: ADOPTION OF INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL REPORTING STANDARD AND VALUE RELEVANCE OF ACCOUNTING INFORMATION IN NIGERIA
summary: This study examined the adoption of international financial reporting standard and value relevance of accounting information in Nigeria. The specific objectives were to determine the effect of PRE-IFRS adoption on the earnings per share of selected companies in Nigeria and to ascertain the effect of POST-IFRS adoption on the earnings per share of selected companies in Nigeria. The study adopted an ex-post facto research design. The population with consists of all listed companies in Nigeria. The sample size for the study consisted of Dangote Sugar Plc, Cussons Nigeria Plc, Nigeria Breweries Plc, and Nestle Nigeria Plc. Data were sourced from the financial statements of Dangote Sugar Plc, Cussons Nigeria Plc, Nigeria Breweries Plc, and Nestle Nigeria Plc. The study was analyzed using panel regression. The findings of this study revealed that PRE-IFRS adoption has a positive and insignificant effect on the earnings per share of selected companies in Nigeria, whereas POST-IFRS adoption has a positive and insignificant effect on the earnings per share of selected companies in Nigeria. In conclusion, the adoption of IFRS tends to enhance the value relevance of accounting information, but its success depends on contextual factors and the commitment of all stakeholders involved in the financial reporting ecosystem of a particular company. The study recommended that companies should ensure that a timely and full implementation of IFRS is implemented to encourage and unlock the actual financial performance benefits accompanied by adopting IFRS in the country.

title: Pengaruh Integrated Reporting Quality, Independent Board, Dan Gender diversity Terhadap Investor Confidence
summary: The growing number of investors in Indonesia’s capital market has not necessarily been accompanied by stable Investor Confidence. Because investors rely substantially on publicly available information, transparent corporate reporting and effective governance are important for limiting information asymmetry and investment uncertainty. Nevertheless, the quality of integrated reporting among Indonesian firms remains uneven, and empirical evidence regarding the roles of Independent Boards and gender diversity in strengthening Investor Confidence is still mixed. This study examines the effects of Integrated Reporting Quality, Independent Board, and gender diversity on Investor Confidence among firms included in the LQ45 Index during 2022–2025. The study covers 25 companies and 100 observations selected using purposive sampling. The findings indicate that Integrated Reporting Quality and Independent Board positively and significantly affect Investor Confidence, whereas gender diversity has a negative but statistically insignificant effect. The contribution of this study is the joint examination of reporting quality and governance mechanisms in explaining Investor Confidence, measured through market responses, within LQ45 companies in Indonesia. The results provide additional evidence on how corporate reporting and governance mechanisms are associated with investor trust.

title: The Effect of Key Audit Matters Disclosures on Stock Price Synchronicity With the Role of Audit Quality in LQ45 Companies from 2022 to 2025
summary: This study examines the impact of Key Audit Matters (KAM) Disclosures on Stock Price Synchronicity and investigates the moderating role of Audit Quality (proxied by Discretionary Accruals The Modified Jones Model) among nonfinancial companies in the LQ45 stock index. Premised on Agency Theory, Signalling Theory, and Efficient Market Hypothesis, this research analyses how the communicative value of expanded auditor reporting influences the integration of firm-specific information into capital market pricing. Through the use of quantitative research approach, this study uses secondary data obtained from the audited financial statements of LQ45 companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2022 to 2025 and stock prices. The data are analyzed using panel data regression with a moderated model, also complemented by Random Effect Model (REM) and White period robust standard errors. The empirical findings reveal that KAM Disclosure has a positive and statistically significant effect on Stock Price Synchronicity, suggesting that greater KAM Disclosures enhance the incorporation of public information into stock prices. Furthermore, Audit Quality has negative and significant effect, indicating that higher Discretionary Accruals (which means lower Audit Quality) weaken the positive relationship between KAM and Stock Price Synchronicity. The findings provide practical implications for companies, auditors, investors, regulators, professional organizations, and future researchers regarding the importance of high-quality financial reporting and informative audit disclosures in supporting efficient capital markets.

summary: Исследование основано на практическом вопросе, с которым всё чаще сталкиваются органы государственного планирования в Центральной Азии: насколько надёжны линейные модели при оценке влияния цифровизации, искусственного интеллекта и факторов устойчивого развития и достаточна ли их предсказательная способность для описания реальных социально-экономических процессов? Для ответа на данный вопрос была сформирована сбалансированная панель данных по 34 развивающимся экономикам и экономикам переходного типа за 2012–2024 гг., включая пять стран Центральной Азии: Узбекистан, Казахстан, Кыргызстан, Таджикистан и Туркменистан. В исследовании использованы открытые базы данных Всемирного банка (World Development Indicators), Международного союза электросвязи (ICT Development Index), Всемирной организации интеллектуальной собственности (Global Innovation Index), а также рейтинги ESG Country Risk. На одном и том же массиве данных были построены две группы моделей. Первая основана на классической эконометрике панельных данных и включает сквозную регрессию методом наименьших квадратов (МНК), модель с фиксированными эффектами и модель со случайными эффектами. Вторая объединяет четыре алгоритма машинного обучения: Ridge и Lasso как регуляризованные линейные модели, а также Random Forest и Gradient Boosting как ансамблевые методы на основе деревьев решений. Качество моделей сравнивалось на отложенной 20%-ной тестовой выборке по трём метрикам: коэффициенту детерминации (R²), среднеквадратичной ошибке и средней абсолютной ошибке. Полученные результаты свидетельствуют о существенном преимуществе модели Gradient Boosting. Она объяснила 96,8% дисперсии ESG-индекса против 81,2% у обычной линейной регрессии, при этом ошибка прогноза сократилась более чем в два раза — с 5,18 до 2,14 пункта. Данное преимущество связано не только с подбором коэффициентов, но и с различиями в природе рассматриваемых моделей: алгоритмы на основе деревьев решений способны выявлять пороговые эффекты и взаимодействия между переменными, которые в линейной спецификации усредняются в рамках единой функциональной зависимости. Расчёт важности признаков показал, что готовность к использованию искусственного интеллекта и уровень цифровизации совместно формируют более половины объясняющей способности модели, опережая по значимости даже ВВП на душу населения. Отдельный раздел статьи посвящён Узбекистану, индекс цифровизации которого за тринадцать лет увеличился почти втрое. На основе полученных результатов сформулированы три практические рекомендации по совершенствованию национальной системы ESG-мониторинга. EN The study is based on a practical question that public planning authorities in Central Asia are increasingly facing: how reliable are linear models in assessing the impact of digitalization, artificial intelligence, and sustainable development factors, and is their predictive capacity sufficient to describe real socio-economic processes? To address this question, a balanced panel dataset covering 34 developing and transition economies for the period 2012–2024 was constructed, including five Central Asian countries: Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan. The study uses open data from the World Bank (World Development Indicators), the International Telecommunication Union (ICT Development Index), the World Intellectual Property Organization (Global Innovation Index), as well as ESG Country Risk ratings. Two groups of models were developed using the same dataset. The first is based on classical panel-data econometrics and includes pooled ordinary least squares (OLS) regression, a fixed-effects model, and a random-effects model. The second group combines four machine-learning algorithms: Ridge and Lasso as regularized linear models, as well as Random Forest and Gradient Boosting as ensemble methods based on decision trees. Model performance was compared on a 20% holdout test sample using three metrics: the coefficient of determination (R²), root mean squared error, and mean absolute error. The results demonstrate a substantial advantage of the Gradient Boosting model. It explained 96.8% of the variance in the ESG index compared with 81.2% for conventional linear regression, while the prediction error decreased by more than half, from 5.18 to 2.14 points. This advantage is associated not only with coefficient estimation but also with fundamental differences in the nature of the models: decision-tree-based algorithms are capable of identifying threshold effects and interactions among variables that are averaged within a single functional relationship in linear specifications. Feature-importance analysis showed that AI readiness and the level of digitalization jointly account for more than half of the model's explanatory power, exceeding even GDP per capita in importance. A separate section of the article focuses on Uzbekistan, whose digitalization index increased almost threefold over thirteen years. Based on the results obtained, three practical recommendations are formulated for improving the national ESG monitoring system. title: Mechanisms Through Which Supply Chain Vertical Integration Improves Corporate Debt Financing Costs: A Multi-Case Study of BYD, NIO and XPeng
summary: Against the backdrop of volatile global raw material prices and supply chain restructuring, the new energy vehicle (NEV) industry exhibits two coexisting modes of supply chain organization, namely vertical integration on the one hand and external procurement or contract manufacturing on the other. Taking BYD as the focal case and NIO and XPeng as comparative cases, and drawing on the three companies’ public annual reports, bond offering circulars, credit rating reports and ESG reports for 2020 to 2025, this paper investigates through which channels supply chain vertical integration affects corporate debt financing costs. The analysis proceeds along the transaction cost line and the information disclosure line, and examines under what conditions digitalization, institutional complexity and ESG performance strengthen or weaken this process. The findings are interpreted on the basis of transaction cost theory and information asymmetry theory, and the divergence in measurement arising from accounting-based indicators of debt cost is clarified.

title: Electronic banking fraud in South Africa: key drivers in the digital age. A qualitative analysis
summary: As South African banks rapidly adopt digital technologies, cybercriminals are exploiting system vulnerabilities with increasingly sophisticated tools, leading to a surge in e-banking fraud.This has resulted in financial losses, reputational damage, and heightened risks to ethical conduct and financial reporting.In response, banks are actively seeking effective defences to protect themselves and their clients from cyberfraud.However, to achieve this overarching aim, it is crucial to understand the underlying drivers of cybercrime and to adopt emerging technologies that uphold financial accountability.The objective of this study was to qualitatively identify the principal drivers of e-banking fraud prevalent within the South African financial system.A qualitative research design was employed, guided by the fraud diamond theory.Semi-structured interviews were selected as the most effective method of data collection, involving 15 purposively chosen senior risk officers from local banks and branches of international banks operating in South Africa.Data analysis was conducted using MAXQDA 24, through which key themes were identified to determine the drivers of e-banking fraud in the South African banking sector.The study found that weak judicial processes, poor internal controls, limited oversight, inadequate investment in new technologies, and low levels of fraud awareness are the primary drivers of e-banking fraud in South Africa.Furthermore, the study highlighted the potential of strategically adopting machine learning for real-time fraud detection, alongside stronger governance, judicial transparency, and sector-wide collaboration.In conclusion, the study recommends that the South African banking sector must urgently address these pressing challenges through the proposed practical measures, thereby enhancing resilience and safeguarding the nation's banking infrastructure, financial stability, reliable financial reports, and client trust in the digital age.
