title: An Assessment of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Reporting Implementation in Public Sector Institutions. A Case Study of the University of Ghana
summary: Abstract This study assessed the implementation of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reporting in public sector institutions, using the University of Ghana as a case study. Specifically, it examined the level of awareness and understanding of ESG reporting, current ESG related practices, implementation challenges, and opportunities for improving transparency and accountability. The study adopted a descriptive qualitative research design. Ten employees with relevant experience in administration, finance, planning, auditing, procurement, sustainability, governance, and quality assurance were purposively selected. Data was collected through semi structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed varying levels of ESG awareness, with employees in strategic administrative and governance roles demonstrating greater understanding. Although the University undertakes several environmental, social, and governance activities, including waste management, energy conservation, student and staff welfare, community engagement, internal auditing, financial accountability, and procurement controls, these activities remain fragmented and are not integrated within a formal ESG reporting framework. Major challenges identified included the absence of an institutional ESG policy, limited expertise and resources, fragmented data systems, inconsistent reporting formats, weak coordination, and inadequate dedicated personnel. Nevertheless, ESG reporting was found to offer significant opportunities for strengthening transparency, accountability, stakeholder confidence, institutional reputation, evidence based decision making, resource allocation, and performance monitoring. The study concludes that effective ESG implementation requires a formal policy, standardized indicators, centralized coordination, staff capacity building, technological support, strong leadership commitment, and active stakeholder participation. These measures would consolidate existing initiatives into a credible, consistent, coordinated, institution wide ESG reporting system.

title: BUREAUCRATIC BARRIERS TO ACCESSING SOCIAL SERVICES AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
summary: Abstract: This article aims to classify the bureaucratic barriers that restrict access to social services within a theoretical framework and to establish under which conditions digital transformation reduces these barriers and under which it reproduces them. The study is a qualitative conceptual analysis. It brings together Weber's theory of bureaucracy, Merton's critique of bureaucratic dysfunction, Lipsky's theory of street-level bureaucracy, the administrative burden and non-take-up approaches, and the literature on digital-era governance, and it examines the cases of Estonia, Denmark, the Netherlands, Australia and Türkiye. Bureaucratic barriers are grouped into six types: information, procedure and documentation, institutional fragmentation, space and time, discretion and attitude, and psychological cost. The findings show that digital transformation largely removes barriers of a technical nature but creates new ones in the form of digital exclusion, the shifting of administrative burden back onto citizens, and algorithmic rigidity. What determines the outcome is not the technology itself but whether the administrative burden is transferred to the state or to the citizen. The article proposes multi-channel service delivery, human oversight, transparency, effective means of appeal and proactive identification of entitlement as the conditions for a digital transformation that widens access.

title: The Effect of Internal Integration on Operational Performance with Supply Chain Capability Mediation
summary: The rapid growth of the coffee shop industry in the Special Region of Yogyakarta has increased competition and requires MSMEs to have efficient and adaptive operational performance. This situation calls for integrated internal process management and supply chain capabilities that are responsive. The setting of this inquiry is coffee shop micro, small, and medium enterprises in the Special Region of Yogyakarta, and it investigates the manner in which internal integration shapes operational performance, positioning supply chain capability as an intervening (mediating) variable. An explanatory quantitative design was adopted, executed through a cross-sectional survey. Two hundred respondents were handpicked via purposive sampling, comprising proprietors, supervisors, and staff members who are personally engaged in operational and supply chain undertakings. Information was gleaned by means of a structured questionnaire and then processed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (SEM-PLS) through the SmartPLS application. The evaluation began with the measurement model, appraised via convergent validity, discriminant validity, and construct reliability, and proceeded to the structural model, which was examined through R-square coefficients and a bootstrapping procedure. According to the empirical findings, internal integration favorably and significantly affects both supply chain capability and operational performance. Supply chain capability, in turn, positively and significantly impacts operational performance and simultaneously functions as a partial mediator connecting internal integration to operational performance. Such outcomes corroborate that fortifying internal integration, buttressed by adaptable supply chain capability, constitutes an indispensable strategy for durably elevating the operational performance of coffee shop MSMEs.

title: Developing an Integrated Procure-to-Pay and Source-to-Contract Digital Framework for Construction Supply Chain Efficiency in Saudi Arabia
summary: Procurement in construction in Saudi Arabia is a highly fragmented process operating across project organisations, specialist contractors and a wide range of dispersed suppliers. This fragmentation means that there is a significant disconnect between the strategic sourcing decisions and the actual transactions that take place in the delivery and payment of materials, equipment and services. This review proposes an integrated digital framework that links Source-to-Contract (S2C) with Procure-to-Pay (P2P), with construction-specific evidence, contractual authority and supplier involvement being the key design constraints. The framework is the result of a structured integrative review of 30 journal papers from the period 2020 to 2025, which were analysed thematically with respect to e-procurement, construction supply chains, information interoperability, payment governance and digital adoption. The review identifies five recurring integration failures: inconsistent master data, separation of contract and operational records, poor linkage of physical progress, fragmented exception handling and uneven levels of organisational readiness. The proposed framework addresses these through the use of a governed supplier and contract register, project coded requisition controls, evidence linked receipt and valuation, invoice reconciliation and an auditable analytics layer. It clearly distinguishes between deterministic control rules and optional advanced technologies (including model based quantity extraction and distributed verification). Performance is assessed in terms of traceability, procurement lead time, first pass match, payment predictability, supplier access and disruption response rather than on the basis of any assumed cost savings. The contribution is a process to data architecture and a staged implementation methodology which is appropriate for Saudi construction programmes, with the boundaries of the approach being clearly defined by procurement regulations, contract provisions and information quality. As the framework is based on a review of the published literature rather than on a live implementation it provides a set of testable design propositions rather than any unproven operational results.

title: Digitisation of Financial Reporting as a Tool for Transparency and Sustainable Business Development in the European Union
summary: Purpose: The study investigates the digitisation of financial reporting as a tool to increase transparency and promote sustainable business development in the context of regulatory transformation in the European Union. Design/Methodology/Approach: The methodological basis is an empirical-analytical design based on secondary data. Quantitative content analysis and technical validation covered 312 corporate financial reports for the 2022–2024 reporting years; tagging, validation errors, completeness, machine readability and logical consistency were assessed for the 243 Inline XBRL reports, and non-financial disclosures were compared across company groups by digitisation level. Research Limitation: The study is limited to EU corporate reports for 2022–2024. Findings: Of the 312 reports, 77.9% were submitted in Inline XBRL format. The average share of tagged items in the primary financial forms was 86.4%. At the same time, only 68.7% of Inline XBRL reports were fully machine-readable and 57.2% were fully logically consistent, indicating a gap between formal digitisation and functional transparency. Companies with a high level of financial reporting digitisation achieved a substantially higher share of fully structured non-financial disclosures than companies with a low level of digitisation. Practical Implication: The results can inform regulatory oversight, corporate digital reporting practices, and transparency standards in the EU. Social Implication: Improved digital reporting supports greater corporate transparency and sustainable business development. Originality/Value: The novelty lies in measuring the gap between formal digitisation and functional transparency in the same reports and in relating digitisation levels to the quality of non-financial disclosures.

title: Green Accounting and Profitability of Listed Manufacturing Firms in Nigeria
summary: This study examined Green Accounting and Profitability of Listed Manufacturing Firms in Nigeria, and considered how green accounting employed by Nigerian firms would significantly impact investors’ return in the long run. The study used ex-post facto research design that covered annual financial report from 2020 to 2024 as listed on Nigerian Exchange Group as at December 31, 2024, and data were analysed through descriptive statistics, regression and Correlation. The findings displayed that return on assets showed significant effect with co-efficient of -41.658 and p-value of 0.035; returns on equity displayed positive but insignificant with co-efficient of 29.182 and P-value of 0.475, and net profit margin showed co-efficient of 265.778 and P-value of 0.001 at 1% level. The study concluded that green accounting was a significant approach that could be used to get more returns on asset utilisation and operational effectiveness. It was recommended that environmental costs should be well managed, adhering to regulatory framework and given tax incentive to firms that involved in sustainability.

title: Unveiling ESG ratings: corporate perspectives and institutionalisation dynamics
summary: Purpose Environmental, social and governance (ESG) ratings have become a central mechanism for assessing, benchmarking and signalling corporate sustainability performance to financial investors. Yet, their widespread use persists despite ongoing criticism of their capacity to accurately reflect firms’ social and environmental contributions. This paper aims to examine this paradox from the perspective of rated companies, exploring why firms continue to engage with ESG ratings despite criticism of their effectiveness, even as investors remain their primary users. Drawing on institutional theory, the authors adopt this underexplored perspective and investigate how ESG ratings become institutionalised within organisations. Design/methodology/approach Based on abductive thematic analysis of 45 semi-structured interviews with sustainability executives from listed European firms, the authors develop a framework distinguishing between substantive and symbolic forms of ESG rating institutionalisation. Findings ESG rating adoption is shaped by institutional pressures and unfolds along a continuum. At one end, firms substantively integrate sustainability considerations into core operations; at the other, ESG ratings are used symbolically to secure external recognition and legitimacy. This study also highlights the risk of deinstitutionalisation if the limitations of ESG ratings remain unaddressed. Practical implications This study offers managers, investors and policymakers insights into navigating ESG pressures and strengthening the credibility of ESG frameworks while providing a diagnostic lens to distinguish symbolic compliance from substantive integration. Social implications While the potential deinstitutionalisation of ESG ratings could erode credibility, accountability and investor trust, substantive adoption could benefit transparency, stakeholder oversight and the diffusion of sustainability norms. Addressing their limitations is therefore crucial for maintaining credibility in the financial sector and directing capital towards companies with meaningful sustainability practices. Originality/value This study extends research on corporate responses to ESG ratings by drawing on institutional theory and developing a conceptual framework of symbolic and substantive institutionalisation from the perspective of rated companies. Specifically, it shifts the explanatory focus beyond firms’ strategic orientations by showing that corporate responses are also shaped by the institutional characteristics and structural limitations of ESG rating systems, thereby advancing the concept of ESG ratings’ deinstitutionalisation.

title: Pengaruh Good Corporate Governance terhadap Kinerja Keuangan pada Sektor Perbankan: Studi Literatur
summary: Tata Kelola Perusahaan yang Baik (GCG) berperan dalam mendukung manajemen perusahaan, termasuk di sektor perbankan, yang tidak hanya dituntut untuk menghasilkan keuntungan. Dalam penerapannya, tata kelola perusahaan bertujuan untuk memastikan bahwa semua aktivitas manajemen yang dilakukan oleh manajemen perusahaan sesuai dengan prinsip akuntabilitas, transparansi, tanggung jawab, dan kehati-hatian. Keberhasilan manajemen perusahaan juga dapat dievaluasi melalui kinerja keuangannya. Penelitian dalam artikel ini dilakukan untuk menguji pengaruh Tata Kelola Perusahaan yang Baik (GCG), yang diukur melalui indikator dewan direksi dan dewan komisaris, terhadap kinerja keuangan, yang diproksikan oleh Return on Assets (ROA), di sektor perbankan. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Tinjauan Pustaka dengan pendekatan Kualitatif Deskriptif melalui Penelitian Pustaka. Hasil penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa GCG memiliki pengaruh yang signifikan terhadap kinerja keuangan. Hal ini karena prinsip-prinsip GCG telah diterapkan oleh perusahaan. Sementara itu, indikator seperti dewan direksi dan dewan komisaris menunjukkan pengaruh positif dan signifikan, artinya hubungan antara manajemen atau dewan direksi dan pemilik perusahaan tetap selaras dalam mencapai tujuan mereka, didukung oleh proses pengawasan dewan komisaris terhadap manajemen perusahaan. Secara teoritis, implikasi studi ini mendukung teori keagenan, yang menjelaskan hubungan antara prinsipal dan agen, khususnya dalam menerapkan GCG yang efektif untuk mengurangi konflik. Sementara itu, dalam praktiknya, penerapan GCG dapat dilakukan oleh manajemen bank untuk meningkatkan kinerja keuangan.

title: Digitalisation de la supply chain : création ou destruction de valeur ? Une revue systématique de la littérature
summary: La digitalisation de la supply chain est souvent présentée comme une source quasi automatique de création de valeur. Les synthèses récentes l’abordent sous l’angle de la performance ou des plateformes, sans articuler simultanément création, captation et destruction de valeur. Pour combler cette lacune, nous examinons dans quelles conditions la digitalisation de la supply chain crée, redistribue ou détruit de la valeur. En s’appuyant sur les recommandations PRISMA 2020, la recherche principale, menée dans ScienceDirect (2015-2026), a identifié 104 références ; 53 articles ont été retenus et complétés par 7 articles issus de recherches exploratoires complémentaires, dont la traçabilité est partielle, soit un corpus de 60 articles en anglais publiés entre 2018 et 2026. L’orientation de la valeur a été codée selon un livre de codes explicite, à partir des résumés pour 53 articles et du texte intégral pour les 7 autres. Dans le corpus constitué, 65 % des articles n’envisagent que la création de valeur, 28 % rapportent des effets ambivalents et 7 % se concentrent sur des effets négatifs ; ce déséquilibre dépend en partie de l’équation de recherche et du codage sur résumés. L’analyse thématique identifie quatre mécanismes de création de valeur (intégration et visibilité, co-création au sein des plateformes, valeur durable, résilience) et quatre mécanismes de destruction ou de redistribution (asymétries de pouvoir, effets non linéaires, disruption des acteurs en place, coûts sociaux), dont l’assise empirique est inégale. L’article propose une typologie croisant niveaux d’analyse et nature des effets, un modèle conceptuel, des propositions testables et un agenda de recherche pour les économies émergentes, notamment maghrébines. Mots clés : digitalisation de la supply chain, création de valeur, destruction de valeur, redistribution de valeur, gouvernance relationnelle, plateformes digitales, économies émergentes, revue systématique.

title: Disclosure incentives, ESG visibility, and market valuation: Evidence from Korea’s Corporate Value-Up Program
summary: Abstract We examine how expanding participation through policy incentives changes the information conveyed by corporate disclosure and whether a firm’s prior environmental, social, and governance (ESG) visibility shapes the market response. The Korea Corporate Value-Up Program offers a useful setting because a December 2025 tax amendment substantially increased participation without changing the underlying disclosure framework. Our analysis covers the full text of 1,086 filings and compares 145 firms that disclosed under the initial voluntary regime with 541 firms that disclosed after the incentive was introduced. Event-study estimates are evaluated against propensity-score-matched non-disclosing firms. The three-day matched-pair cumulative average abnormal return is 1.008 percentage points before the amendment but only 0.005 percentage points afterward. During the voluntary period, announcement returns are smaller for firms with higher prior ESG ratings, suggesting that disclosure provides less new information when a firm is already closely followed. Once participation becomes widespread, the announcement effect disappears. Instead, investors respond to the specificity of disclosed commitments, but only when those commitments come from firms with higher ESG ratings. These findings show that disclosure operates through two distinct channels: the decision to disclose and the credibility of what is disclosed. Policies that increase participation may therefore broaden disclosure coverage while weakening participation itself as a market signal.

title: Barriers to Blockchain Adoption in Circular Supply Chain Management: A Systematic Review and TISM-MICMAC Analysis
summary: This study examines the practical challenges organizations encounter in adopting blockchain for circular supply chain management.The objective is to provide actionable insights for managers and policymakers to facilitate blockchain adoption for strengthening circularity within supply chains and enhancing circular supply chain performance.A comprehensive systematic literature review is conducted with 34 articles to identify key barriers.Subsequently, the key barriers were modeled using inputs from nine experts through Total Interpretive Structural Modelling (TISM) and MICMAC analysis.The results indicate that barriers such as lack of government regulations and lack of stakeholder involvement function as root-level drivers, while mid-level feedback barriers include cost, lack of trust, and lack of standardization.At the upper level, outcome barriers such as security, privacy, and scalability emerge as dependent effects.The findings highlight that successful blockchain adoption in circular supply chains requires first strengthening institutional and collaborative foundations, followed by addressing technical limitations.Overall, the study emphasizes realworld implementation considerations and the adoption of circular economy principles within blockchain-enabled supply chain transformation.

title: Évolution de la recherche sur la Responsabilité Sociétale des Organisations : une revue bibliométrique (2015-2025)
summary: Résumé La Responsabilité Sociétale des Entreprises (RSE) s’est progressivement imposée comme un champ de recherche majeur dans les sciences de gestion et les sciences sociales, en raison de l’importance croissante accordée aux enjeux de durabilité, de gouvernance responsable et d’engagement des parties prenantes. Dans ce contexte, la multiplication des publications scientifiques rend nécessaire l’utilisation d’approches analytiques permettant de structurer et de synthétiser la littérature existante.L’objectif de cette étude est d’analyser l’évolution de la recherche scientifique consacrée à la RSE à travers une approche bibliométrique. Les données bibliographiques ont été extraites de la plateforme Dimensions AI, et les analyses ont été réalisées à l’aide du logiciel VOSviewer afin de cartographier les réseaux scientifiques et d’identifier les principales dynamiques de recherche.Les résultats mettent en évidence une croissance significative de la production scientifique relative à la RSE au cours de la dernière décennie. L’analyse révèle également l’existence de réseaux de collaboration structurés, ainsi que la présence de plusieurs thématiques dominantes, notamment la gouvernance d’entreprise, la durabilité organisationnelle, l’engagement des parties prenantes et les critères ESG.Cette étude contribue à une meilleure compréhension de la structure intellectuelle du champ de la RSE en identifiant les auteurs, institutions et revues les plus influents, ainsi que les principales orientations de la recherche. Elle met également en évidence certaines lacunes dans la littérature, notamment la sous-représentation de certains contextes géographiques, ce qui ouvre des perspectives pour de futures recherches.Mots clés : Responsabilité Sociétale des Entreprises (RSE) ; Gouvernance d’entreprise durable; Pratiques commerciales responsables. Abstract Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) has progressively emerged as a major field of research in management and social sciences, due to the growing importance attributed to sustainability challenges, responsible governance, and stakeholder engagement. In this context, the rapid increase in scientific publications highlights the need for analytical approaches capable of structuring and synthesizing the existing body of literature.The objective of this study is to analyze the evolution of scientific research related to CSR through a bibliometric approach. Bibliographic data were extracted from the Dimensions AI platform, and the analysis was conducted using VOSviewer to map scientific networks and identify the main research dynamics within the field.The results reveal a significant growth in scientific production related to CSR over the past decade. The analysis also highlights the existence of structured collaboration networks as well as several dominant research themes, including corporate governance, organizational sustainability, stakeholder engagement, and ESG criteria.This study contributes to a better understanding of the intellectual structure of the CSR field by identifying the most influential authors, institutions, and journals, as well as the main research trends. It also highlights certain gaps in literature, particularly the underrepresentation of specific geographical contexts, thereby opening new perspectives for future research.Keywords : Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) ; Sustainable Corporate Governance ; Responsible Business Practices.

title: ADOPTION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT: BARRIERS AND ENABLERS IN DEVELOPING ECONOMIES
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology capable of enhancing efficiency, decision-making, and resilience in supply chain management. However, its adoption in developing economies remains constrained by several technological, organizational, and environmental challenges. This study examined the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management, with emphasis on the barriers and enablers in developing economies, using Nigeria as the study context. A cross-sectional survey research design was adopted, and data were collected from 235 employees, managers, and supply chain professionals in selected manufacturing firms, logistics companies, retail organizations, and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria using a structured questionnaire titled Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Supply Chain Management Index (AIASCMI). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson Product Moment Correlation. The findings revealed that identified barriers, including inadequate digital infrastructure, high implementation costs, shortage of skilled personnel, and organizational challenges, have a significant negative relationship with the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. The study also found that identified enablers, such as top management support, technological readiness, employee competence, and government support, significantly influence the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence. The study concludes that overcoming existing barriers while strengthening organizational and technological capabilities is essential for the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. It is recommended that organizations invest in digital infrastructure, workforce development, and supportive management practices to maximize the benefits of Artificial Intelligence and improve supply chain performance.

title: Impact of Digital Leadership on Digital Transformation Readiness in MSMEs: A Review
summary: The contemporary business environment is characterised by unprecedented volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity (VUCA), making digital transformation readiness a strategic imperative for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) that constitute over 90% of all businesses globally and employ approximately 60–70% of the workforce. This conceptual review paper examines the impact of digital leadership on digital transformation readiness in MSMEs, with particular focus on Nigeria and Kano State. The main aim is to synthesise existing theoretical and empirical evidence and develop an integrated conceptual framework positioning the three dimensions of digital leadership digital vision and strategic foresight, technological enablement and dynamic capabilities, and innovation facilitation and empowerment as antecedents of digital transformation readiness comprising technological readiness, organisational readiness, and environmental readiness. The study adopted a systematic conceptual review design following adapted PRISMA guidelines, searching eight academic databases (Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, EBSCOhost, Emerald Insight, ScienceDirect, JSTOR, and ProQuest) for the period January 2015 to December 2025. The review integrated dynamic capabilities theory (Teece, 2007), transformational leadership theory (Bass & Avolio, 1994), and technology-organisation-environment (TOE) framework (Tornatzky & Fleischer, 1990) into a unified framework adapted to Nigerian and Kano contexts. Policymakers (SMEDAN, Kano State Enterprise Development Agency) should design training addressing all three dimensions and address infrastructural deficits through solar-powered digital hubs. Development organisations should reallocate resources toward innovation empowerment given high failure rates. The framework offers eighteen testable propositions to guide future empirical research in resource-constrained environments.

title: Linking green entrepreneurship to green innovation: the mediating role of green entrepreneurial self-efficacy
summary: Purpose In line with the United Nations 2030 Agenda, environmental sustainability has become a prominent concept in academic discourse. Due to its vast natural resources, Africa is well-positioned to become a global leader in green business. However, with a growing small and medium-sized enterprise (SME)population in Africa, empirical evidence on SME sustainability efforts remains limited. For this reason, this research examined the mediation effect of green entrepreneurial self-efficacy on the relationship between green entrepreneurship and green innovation in Zimbabwean manufacturing SMEs. Design/methodology/approach The data were analysed using SmartPLS 4 from a randomly selected sample of 370 managers. Findings The results showed that while green entrepreneurship strongly influenced green innovation, green entrepreneurial self-efficacy partially mediated the relationship between the two variables. Originality/value The study contributes context-specific evidence from an African economy, addressing the limited representation of developing markets in green innovation research. In environments characterised by institutional constraints and resource scarcity, identifying self-efficacy as an enabling mechanism provides novel insight into how firms can stimulate green innovation despite structural limitations. The findings, therefore, enrich both theory and practice by integrating strategic and psychological perspectives within the African economic context.

title: Pengaruh ESG Disclosure, Gender Diversity dan Board Size terhadap Nilai Perusahaan Dimoderasi Profitabilitas
summary: This study aims to examine and analyze the impact of ESG disclosure, gender diversity, and board size on firm value, while simultaneously testing profitability as a moderating variable across infrastructure companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2021-2024 period. Employing a purposive sampling approach, the research sample comprises 30 companies, yielding a total of 120 firm-year observations. The analytical framework utilizes panel data regression integrated with Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) under the Random Effect Model (REM). Empirical findings reveal that gender diversity has a positive and statistically significant effect on firm value. In contrast, ESG disclosure and board size show no significant influence on firm value. Furthermore, the moderation assessment confirms that profitability moderates and weakens the positive link between gender diversity and firm value. Nevertheless, profitability fails to moderate the effects of ESG disclosure or board size on firm value. Conclusively, these results imply that capital market investors in the infrastructure sector value gender diversity more heavily than ESG disclosure or board size

title: The Relationship Between Financial Managers’ Leadership Style and the Quality of Financial Reporting in Organizations
summary: This study was conducted to examine the relationship between financial managers’ leadership style and the quality of financial reporting in organizations. This research is applied in terms of purpose and descriptive-correlational in terms of implementation method. The statistical population consisted of all financial managers, accountants, and auditors employed in organizations. A sample of 212 participants was selected using stratified random sampling. Data were collected using the standardized Multifactor Leadership Questionnaire (MLQ) and the Financial Reporting Quality Questionnaire developed by Kawasi (2021). Data analysis was performed at both descriptive and inferential levels using Structural Equation Modeling based on the Partial Least Squares approach (PLS-SEM) through SmartPLS version 3 software. The results indicated a positive and strong relationship between transformational leadership style and financial reporting quality (β = 0.552, t-value = 8.899), a positive and moderate relationship between transactional leadership style and financial reporting quality (β = 0.358, t-value = 3.429), and a negative and weak relationship between laissez-faire leadership style and financial reporting quality (β = -0.259, t-value = 2.675). All relationships were statistically significant at the 95% confidence level. Financial managers who adopt a transformational leadership style, characterized by inspirational motivation, intellectual stimulation, and individualized consideration, can significantly enhance the quality of financial reporting. In contrast, the laissez-faire leadership style exerts an adverse effect on reporting quality. Therefore, emphasizing transformational leadership competencies in the selection and development of financial managers is recommended as a key behavioral factor for improving the transparency and reliability of financial information.

title: Selecting the right path: a framework for lead-time reduction in consumer goods supply chains
summary: Purpose Consumer goods firms often face severe shortages caused by forecast inaccuracy, where a few variants become unexpected bestsellers and trigger costly stockouts. This article positions the choice of lead-time reduction initiatives as a crucial decision for enhancing responsiveness and mitigating shortages and frames this decision as a performance-management prioritization problem under uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach This work developed a pragmatic direction-selection framework grounded in a design science approach and applied in a case to guide managers in evaluating and prioritizing lead-time reduction initiatives. The framework integrates insights from the literature with feasibility-oriented evaluation criteria, applying the principles of multi-criteria decision analysis to assess initiatives in terms of expected return on investment (impact relative to effort) and implementation horizon. Findings The study offers a theory-based, empirically validated framework for identifying and planning lead time reduction initiatives in a context of hard-to-predict demand, making explicit a performance-management logic for prioritizing responsiveness initiatives. The case shows that initiatives with attractive expected impact–effort profiles are not necessarily robust priorities once implementation risk and sensitivity to assumptions are considered. Research limitations/implications The study advances performance-management research by reframing lead-time reduction as a decision problem under uncertainty and extending the focus from performance evaluation to intervention selection, translating dispersed responsiveness insights into a replicable prioritization logic, validated in a real case and supported by sensitivity checks. Practical implications The study provides a stepwise decision-support tool that helps cross-functional teams prioritize feasible lead-time reduction initiatives and translate them into an implementation plan, with risk and sensitivity checks to avoid assumption-driven choices. Originality/value The paper offers a validated innovative decision-support framework that operationalizes lead-time reduction as a performance-management choice under demand uncertainty, using an explicit prioritization logic to select responsiveness initiatives end-to-end.
